## Mathematical conventions and corrections

The paper keeps the full indexed peripheral source maps, their conjugacy ambiguities and the orientation line. It distinguishes a prescribed section homomorphism from its image subgroup by explicitly writing the quotient labels. Discrete, full profinite and pro-p maps have separate domains, and every use of a completion map includes its injectivity or exactness argument. The first page gives the global notation concordance. Each numbered assertion is followed by section/folio/scan metadata; numerical evidence for a transcription alternative appears in the separate readings register and is never called a settled reading.

Several corrections drive the later proofs. The sphere with three punctures has free group of rank two, so the abelian bound on scan116 is nu<=2. The torus requires the same extension-class correction as the annulus. A reflection section can extend to different maximal finite stabilizers; the explicit type(0,3) NEC amalgam proves this in the discrete group and its completion. A finite subgroup of the mapping class group does not determine an exceptional-type affine extension: the retained extension has to be part of the index. Arbitrary functors between peripheral categories also include maps induced by no surface homeomorphism; C.1 gives the exact core restriction used in the proved equivalence. Finite-point drilling removes isolated rotation stabilizers but leaves mirror arcs; C.14 records the resulting obstruction rather than treating a reflection as a rotation.

The peripheral category uses E/L_i with the specified right action of E_i/L_i. The proposed E/E_i replacement loses the map to the operator group; C.2 gives an actual double-cover example and a finite certificate. The abstract-presentation question retains the phrase that the displayed relation generates all relations. The same numbered result gives a complete counterexample to a weaker proposed shortcut: the closed torsion-free Polish group of integer-valued L1 functions modulo constant integers has fundamental group Z. Support compression contracts its universal cover, and the indicator-function loop generates its fundamental group. Integer medians give its closed isometric embedding into L1 modulo real constants; dual-ball evaluation, Cantor pullback, interpolation and an explicit tanh shear then embed it closedly into the disc homeomorphism group. Its loop contracts in the larger real shear group. This proves that closedness and torsion-freeness alone cannot give the required fundamental-group injection. The corollary to C.39 now excludes its realization as an exact full centralizer: every centralizer containing this abelian subgroup contracts its generating loop, so inclusion induces the zero map on its fundamental group Z. Equality with that centralizer would induce an isomorphism. This closes that particular proposed counterexample route while retaining the general C.12 obligation.

C.27 gives a conjugacy-natural median contraction for every loop in a line centralizer, allowing orientation reversal by the operators. C.28 proves the orbit classification for a group generated by a compact plane loop: open orbits, points, Jordan curves, and intrinsic lines. The proof uses compact Peano exhaustions, the winding-number argument for a moving Jordan curve, and the countability of dendrite branch points together with transitivity; it does not assume a foliation. The line parametrization embeds every compact interval and makes the restricted loop compact-open continuous, while retaining possible global accumulation of the orbit.

C.29 proves the injective winding map for every circle centralizer and its natural zero-winding contraction. Evaluation at two points of a Jordan curve gives an exact difference-angle winding equal to the circle winding; the canonical hyperbolic plane loop is ambient-null, so every circle orbit has zero winding. C.30 proves that the centralizer of a transitive Polish action on a surface is locally compact and acts freely and properly. Its application to an open orbit uses the closure of the actual restricted operator image, retaining the kernel and its topology. C.31 proves uniform track control at common fixed points and the exact inverse-loop identity for the median. C.32 proves the discrete proper open-orbit case by a quotient-surface contraction and its specified covering lift. C.33 proves every proper closed-operator case, using the faithful product action for the Hilbert–Smith theorem, the free-action slice theorem and explicit coordinates in each Lie-group dimension. In dimension one it retains every component and the possible inversion, removes the translation cocycle by an explicit function, and contracts the resulting function and base-homeomorphism factors. Thus every individual orbit is handled intrinsically.

C.34 proves continuity on the entire closed nonopen locus. A folded nearby arc produces a cap whose two first-exit endpoints lie outside a small rectangle. A short original-loop segment moves the nonfixed limit point across the cap extremum while its whole track remains in the rectangle, a contradiction to intrinsic path continuity. This no-excess argument gives convergence of intervals, prefix endpoints and medians. Circle limits use only a lift of the compact point-track to a collar and local lifts inside a single covering rectangle. The inverse-loop identity proves joint continuity of the inverse family. Hyperbolic loops with no open lifted orbit therefore contract in the exact original centralizer by deck descent. C.35 supplies an exact obstruction to extending this fixed median prescription. The positive-diagonal action on a simplex has interior translation coordinates(a,b) and edge characters a,b,a-b. Doubling the simplex and removing one fixed vertex gives a plane action. The parameter loop0→(1,1)→(1,0)→0 is globally equivariantly contractible by scaling. At one median parameter its edge translations are(1,0,0), outside the exact restriction image(A,B,A-B); the annihilator residual is1. Every equivariant interior map, including one exchanging the two sheets, has that restriction image. Thus a successful global proof must allow changing the nonopen-locus contraction. C.36 advances the frontier comparison: the closure of the loop-generated group maps by an actual open Polish quotient onto the two-dimensional simply transitive Lie centralizer. Its kernel fixes the entire orbit closure, so the quotient acts continuously there. The based universal-cover exponential contraction descends to that closure. Every shared boundary orbit has exactly the same effective Lie image from both sides, and the quotient homomorphisms intertwine the unique based lifts and exponentials. Thus these contractions agree on overlaps and glue with continuous inverse on every finite union. C.37 supplies the uniform continuity at infinitely accumulating closures described next. Compatible extension to the exterior of their closed union, including the dimension-zero/one operator images and the remaining nonopen strata, remains C.12.

C.37 proves the contraction on X2, the entire closure of the union of dimension-two proper operator open orbits. The exact input is a three-word equation: every fractional endpoint in R² or the simply connected positive affine group is a path difference, or its product with the endpoint. The signed-measure theorem of Grandoni–Ravi–Singh–Zenklusen, author-version Theorem4.7 and Section4.3.2, gives the planar equation for polygonal paths; uniform approximation gives every continuous path. Explicit affine coordinates turn left multiplication by the endpoint flow into horizontal translation. The equality is retained in the universal covering group. Actual plane word isotopies then lie in one compact family. On every nonopen limit orbit the metabelian identity passes from the open orbits, and the path-connected transitive image is proved to be R, S1 or the positive affine group. For each integer n, the residual of the nth power after removing floor(nr) endpoint powers remains a three-word element. Bounded logarithms force the exact fractional limit on lines. On circles, a residual word loop is null in every approximating Lie group; its two-point configuration winding passes to the limit, so the residual equation holds over R and retains the full winding integer. Density proves joint continuity throughout X2, and the inverse loop proves inverse continuity. This resolves the infinite-accumulation issue for that closed set. Its contraction still needs compatible extension to the exterior of X2; the median prescription there cannot be assumed compatible, by C.35.

C.38 proves that the full compact-open centralizer of a transitive nonabelian action on a line or circle is discrete cyclic: trivial or infinite cyclic on a line, finite cyclic on a circle. The evaluation map is an explicit homeomorphism onto a closed normalizer quotient. The proper free action yields the actual regular covering. In the plane problem the exact restriction sequence retains the operator stabilizer, its kernel and its discrete image; no continuity from an inherited plane topology to a recurrent intrinsic line topology is assumed. This supplies the stated one-dimensional quotients, while the transverse relative-extension problem in C.12 remains.

C.39 supplies a complete global contraction for ambient-null plane loops with pairwise commuting values. On each intrinsic orbit the closure is a free transitive abelian Lie group, and the actual loop-generated image equals that closure. The based universal-cover lift has zero endpoint. One compact family of actual three-word plane isotopies represents every scaled endpoint on every orbit type. At a mixed-type limit, nth powers minus floor(nr) endpoint powers have uniformly bounded word representatives. Line translations give the exact real limit; on circles the residual word loop has zero two-point winding, so the real lifted equation holds with its winding integer retained. Every word limit therefore has the required fractional action. Applying the same argument to the inverse loop gives joint inverse continuity. The disk filling lifts through the explicit map D2 times the universal covering surface; each commutator with an operator lift or deck transformation is a continuous deck-valued function equal to the identity at the base point. Descent supplies the contraction on every connected admissible surface. On hyperbolic surfaces every commuting-valued centralizer loop contracts. This proof does not replace an arbitrary loop by a commuting-valued representative; that reduction, or a general compatible extension, remains the exact C.12 issue.

C.40 proves the further case of a loop whose generated closure is locally compact in the actual induced homeomorphism-group topology. That closure is connected and lies in the closed centralizer. Its faithful action on the surface times R makes it a Lie group by the checked Hilbert–Smith theorem. Borel’s exact multiplication coordinates K times R^d give an identity-fixing deformation into a connected compact subgroup. Haar averaging gives a bi-invariant metric; its universal cover is geodesically complete by the explicit connection formula. A geodesic to the lifted endpoint of the loop projects to a one-parameter loop in the same based homotopy class. The entire homotopy stays in the centralizer, and C.39 contracts that representative when the original ambient class vanishes. Thus each locally compact centralizer has injective fundamental-group comparison, and every such closure case on a hyperbolic surface has trivial loop class. Root opened Borel’s original scan and visually checked the product formula on printed page271; sections3–4, pages277–278, give the stated reductions. The general closure need not satisfy the local compactness hypothesis established for this result; no change of topology is made.

C.41 proves the fundamental-group injection for arbitrary operator subgroups with a dense orbit on every connected admissible surface. In the plane, the union of open loop-generated orbits is operator-invariant. A dense operator orbit meets every such open orbit O, and its intersection with O is exactly one orbit of the O-stabilizing operators. Their proper closed image has a closed orbit containing that dense subset, so it is transitive and two-dimensional. The whole open-orbit union is consequently the dimension-two union of C.37, and its closure is the plane. With no open orbits, C.34 already gives the contraction. For a general surface, the exact ambient disk family lifts, and the full group of operator lifts has a dense orbit equal to the inverse image of the original one. The plane contraction descends. This proof requires no local compactness assumption on the original operator group or on the global loop-generated closure. C.12 remains for general actions without a dense orbit and loops for which the other proved reductions have not been obtained.

## Proof details requiring particular care

### Closed solvable groups: A.19

The initial partial bound C_{P_m}(H) subset P_m^[m-1] is retained in A.18, but the obstruction is resolved by A.19. The proof starts with an explicit continuous Magnus homomorphism F→R^r⋊F_ab. Its kernel is proved to be F″ by factoring every finite metabelian quotient through a finite wreath embedding. Thus no exactness of an unspecified completed cellular chain complex is assumed.

For the surface relator, its image is the Fox vector v=(1-b1,a1-1,…,1-bg,ag-1). The closed normal relator module is exactly Rv, because Rv is a compact image. This proves the injection P′/P″→R^(2g)/Rv. Multiplication by a1^n-1 is injective on this quotient: the independent a2-1 coordinate is a nonzerodivisor modulo a1^n-1. Both nonzerodivisor assertions are proved by finite-coefficient cyclic orbit sums; choosing M divisible by the Sigma-part of n and passing from C_M to C_{kM} makes each orbit fibre sum k equal coefficients modulo k. This explicitly includes p=2,3 and integers n divisible by p.

Finite class-two groups with commutator module (wedge²A)/(sum a_i wedge b_i) force the abelianization of a centralizer element onto the selected generator's line. This proves the metabelian base case. For higher depth, every finite abelian cover has a lift x^d of the selected nonseparating simple curve. Its integral homology pushes forward to d[x], so it is again nonseparating and can be made a standard handle generator. A.15 justifies both required intersections of closed derived subgroups and products. Induction proves all depths, and two independent standard-generator powers then prove slimness.

This proof does not establish the broader arbitrary-characteristic assertion discussed as unknown in the supplied Yamaguchi preprint. It establishes exactly the characteristic-zero topological surface groups requested here. No priority claimed.

### One-puncture peripheral threshold: A.16

Finite abelian covers of a once-punctured surface have at least three cusps after choosing the cofinal family of deck degrees>=3. In the cusp homology module Z_Sigma^Q/Z_Sigma(sum e_q), an equality n e_q=a e_1 forces q=1 and a=n. This puts every peripheral power-centralizer into the derived subgroup. At depth2 that subgroup is abelian and is the entire centralizer. At depth>=3 the same cover makes c a primitive free-basis element, so the finite-rank free theorem at one smaller depth applies. A.15 then descends the result back to the original quotient. The strict metabelian inclusion is certified by explicit UT4 matrices at p=2,3,5 and by the same symbolic matrix calculation at any p in Sigma.

### Exact source applications

- Mochizuki–Tamagawa, Definition1.2, Remark1.2.2 and Proposition1.4 apply to hyperbolic geometric surface groups over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field and an arbitrary nontrivial full formation. The ordinary/full/pro-p presentation comparisons and the deduction of torsion-freeness from finite p-cohomological dimension are written out.
- Mochizuki2004 Lemma1.3.7 gives commensurable terminality for both full and pro-l cusp inertia. A centralizer of an integer power lies in that commensurator, giving A.7.
- Mochizuki2007 Proposition1.2(i) identifies underlying edges when an intersection is open in one. It does not literally identify arbitrary chosen conjugate subgroup representatives. A.5 therefore proves its one-sided transporter assertion using exact power-centralizers and compact recurrence, with no strengthened quotation of Proposition1.2(i).
- Closed base-loop centralizers in the unquotiented completion are obtained twice, from Boggi–Zalesskii2019 Proposition3.6 and from Mochizuki2007 Proposition1.2(ii) after a one-node degeneration. Genus2 is checked explicitly: its normalization has genus1 and two inverse branches, hence remains stable and hyperbolic.
- The finite-rank part of Yamaguchi2026 Theorem1.5 is used in A.14. Its finite semidirect-product step, metabelian module step and descent to finite abelian covers were read. No infinite-rank limiting argument is imported. A.17 independently checks the cover/transfer proof of the centre and torsion statements. A.19 independently proves the precise Magnus embedding used in the closed argument.
- Yagasaki's actual supplied TeX was read. The compact marked-surface case needed for A.12 lies in Lemma2.1; the finite marked set is a compact subpolyhedron. We also read Theorem1.1 and the local-extension theorem. This avoids treating a statement about diffeomorphisms as one about compact-open homeomorphisms without a comparison.
- Farb–Margalit Theorem4.6 includes punctures/boundary and has an explicit extended-group remark. Theorem8.8 is the extended punctured Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem. A.12 uses the inverse-track convention needed to make point-pushing a homomorphism and checks its induced inner automorphism. The book's p235 informal phrase about a unique representative fixing the distinguished loop is not used: conjugation by that loop supplies many representatives. The quotient automorphism is unique because those residual conjugations die upon filling.

## Corrections and typed comparisons

The bracket nu<=3 on scan116 is false at the pair of pants; the correct bound is nu<=2. The rank2g+nu-1 requires nu>=1. The admitted plane retains its noninjective peripheral source map, while the closed sphere is excluded from the nontrivial orientation-by-group-cohomology definition. The early cohomological orientation marking is related to the later covariant orientation line by an explicit dual map, rather than an unmarked inversion of its character.

The torus needs the same H² extension-class correction as the annulus. The pure orientation-preserving index on scan189 is exactly2nu!, where nu counts the old punctures. In the abelian filling exception, forgetting annulus peripheral indices and orientation loses a C2; retaining the complete data restores the four-element target and the isomorphism. The scan194 abelian labels refer to filled types; both drilled groups there are F2.

The phrase relation génératrice on scan318 gives the full profinite presentation, hence the explicit isomorphism to the standard completion. The Zhat² example refutes only the weakened requirement that a generating tuple satisfy the equation. It is not presented as a counterexample to the actual full-presentation axiom.

A.20 has all four domains and the completion comparison maps written out. The discrete filling isomorphism gives an isomorphism of the full completions of the two discrete automorphism groups. It also gives the commutative square with the separately defined normalized filling map on all continuous automorphisms. Neither vertical surjectivity nor a bottom-arrow isomorphism is needed for A(d). For odd p the proposed replacement of the upper full completions by pro-p completions has an explicit obstruction: an orientation-reversing involution is killed in a pro-p group while acting by -1 on the pro-p orientation line.

## Corrections carrying consequences for other parts

- The unique maximal-section assertion requires a nontrivial positive part. Reflections already violate it in the smallest hyperbolic type (0,3). The same concrete discrete subgroups survive in the completion.
- The valid positive discrete normalizer equality N=C does not make the torsion in C into a group. The explicit punctured-torus example separates these claims by their actual inclusion and product maps.
- The scan-179 uniqueness expectation fails for a free glide involution as well as for C_n×C2 of arbitrary order.
- An outer subgroup in an abelian type does not determine its lift extension. The same order-two subgroup in GL2Z has a two-section realization and a zero-section realization.
- Formula (52) presents a group with a free F_g factor. The quotient F_g→Z^g, with its explicit equivariant abelianization map, is the correction needed to obtain the stated geometric semidirect product.

# Full profinite recognition: Haran's rank-three construction and peripheral test

We searched directly for torsion-free virtually free full profinite groups and opened the complete original Dan Haran article, *Non-free torsion-free profinite groups with open free subgroups*, Israel Journal of Mathematics50(4)(1985),350–352. Its unnumbered Proposition provides a counterexample for every free open rank at least three. We reconstructed the first case, rank three and index two, rather than relying on the proposition alone.

The reconstruction starts with H=Fhat(l,a,b), epsilon_3=−1 and epsilon_p=1 at other primes, and kappa_2=1 with the other kappa-components zero. The formulas alpha(l)=l^epsilon, alpha(a)=b, alpha(b)=l^kappa a l^(−kappa) satisfy alpha²=Inn(l^kappa), alpha(l^kappa)=l^kappa. The paper writes the complete associative multiplication on H times C2. It identifies the subgroup generated by l and the coset lift with the explicit mixed-prime virtually procyclic group, constructs a retraction onto it, and proves torsion-freeness of the full extension.

The group maps onto (C3)^2 semidirect C2 by inversion. This quotient needs three generators, whereas a free profinite group with a rank-three subgroup of index two would have rank two. The independent Python standard-library program `haran_rank3.py` executes all5832 associativity checks and all324 ordered-pair generation checks in this18-element quotient. Pair-generated subgroup orders1,2,3,6,9 have counts1,27,32,216,48. Three displayed generators generate all18 elements.

The surface peripheral hypothesis is tested explicitly. For type(1,2), every loop-preserving involution has determinant on first homology equal to the sign of the puncture permutation: its cusp multiplier is lambda times that sign, and the filled torus determinant is lambda, with lambda²=1. Haran's outer action instead has determinant−epsilon, a sign varying with the prime. This excludes every type(1,2) marking on this kernel.

For type(0,4), we chose the free basis l,a,b^epsilon and fourth loop (l*a*b^epsilon)^(-1). The first three loops have the required action. The fourth fails: mapping l to(12), a to(23), and b to(123) in S3 sends P=l*a*b^epsilon to1 but sends alpha(P) to(123). The actual exponent residues are epsilon=5 and kappa=3 modulo6. The program exhausts all216 assignments and records24 failures, including this one.

These first tests establish the nonfree underlying extension and exclude the displayed peripheral candidate. D.29 subsequently constructs a different invariant (0,4) marking and supplies an exact isomorphism to this extension, completing the counterexample to D(d). The basis-independent restrictions and the finite failures below remain part of its verification.

Files: `haran_rank3.tex`, `haran_rank3_results.json`, `haran_rank3_references.bib`, and the Python program with JSON and stdout outputs. The failed initial debugging assertion that every pair generated at most six elements was corrected before the successful execution: two independent elements of the normal(C3)^2 generate nine elements. The proof treats the two cases separately and the final output contains the full histogram.

## Further basis-independent restriction and a second finite certificate

For every invariant type-(0,4) marking, the trace on ordinary first homology forces either a single transposition with multiplier epsilon, or a double transposition with multiplier minus epsilon; the identity permutation is already impossible modulo 3. The canonical character sending every cusp generator to -1 is one of the three alpha-invariant characters chi1=(-1,1,1), chi2=(1,-1,-1), chi3=(-1,-1,-1) on (l,a,b).

The explicit cocycle matrix in (D.26g) gives determinants 1, -epsilon_p, 1 on the three two-dimensional twisted H1 spaces. The all-cusp-negative double cover is of type (1,4); restriction identifies twisted H1 with its anti-invariant part, and filling identifies this with H1 of a torus. All maps are stated and their equivariance checked, so its determinant equals the original peripheral multiplier. At p=3 this excludes every single-transposition marking. At p=5 the double-transposition case requires chi2. Thus only the double-transposition case with multiplier -epsilon and character chi2 remains.

The explicit candidate (a,b^(-epsilon),b^epsilon*l,(a*l)^(-1)) has exactly those necessary properties but its third cusp condition reduces to a^epsilon*l^epsilon being conjugate to (a*l)^epsilon. In S4, epsilon is 5 modulo 12. Taking a=(2 3 4), l=(1 2 3 4), b=1 gives the transposition (1 4) versus the four-cycle (1 3 2 4). The executed program tests every one of the 576 ordered S4 pairs and finds 96 nonconjugacy witnesses. It also checks all six twisted cocycle matrices over F3 and F5, fixed coboundary lines, and the scalar action of the square on the quotient.

The two finite candidates are excluded. The construction in D.29, described next, supplies a different double-transposition marking satisfying all the necessary conditions proved here.

## Resolution by D.29

The earlier arbitrary-marking obstruction has now been resolved affirmatively. D.29 chooses a genuine three-cusp automorphism tau with multiplier lambda=-epsilon and glues it to Inn(l^kappa) tau^(-1) on the two complementary pants. The resulting outer involution preserves the complete tuple (a,a^(-1)l,b,b^(-1)l^(-1)). Its basis (l,a,b'=tau(a)) identifies the extension exactly with the Haran extension proved above: alpha(l)=l^epsilon, alpha(a)=b', alpha(b')=l^kappa a l^(-kappa). Thus the nonfree torsion-free extension does admit an invariant full (0,4) marking, completing the counterexample to full profinite recognition. All necessary conditions and finite failures recorded earlier remain valid for their specified candidates.


# D.28: prime-order sections and exact fixed-subgroup comparison

The full proof is in `gt_torsion_sections.tex`. Its input is a homomorphism from C_p to the actual full profinite GT_0 whose p-adic multiplier is one, which includes every odd prime p. The normalized GT_0 representation is itself a homomorphism into Aut(Fhat2), so the semidirect product used here has the given order-p action without an additional lifting assumption.

The three cusp normalizer extensions split. This is proved through the exact map E → F2^(p) × C_p, then an explicit coordinatewise solution of the cyclic norm equation. At the prime p the required exponent is divisible by p because of that quotient map; at another prime the norm is either p, a unit, or zero with a necessarily zero target exponent.

The profinite Brown theorem gives the finite equality

    sum over section classes (1 + dim H1(fixed subgroup,F_p)) = dim H^n(E,F_p) <= 3.

Each cusp section contributes at least two because its fixed subgroup contains the p-primary component of a primitive cusp and a nonzero restricted homology functional detects it. Thus all cusp sections are conjugate. Two independent cusp classes then force that one fixed subgroup to have first cohomology dimension at least two, exhausting the bound. There are no other section classes. The actual closed fixed subgroup C is projective and its maximal pro-p quotient has rank two. Its map to F2^(p) is onto by the two independent cusp images and hence is an isomorphism. This section establishes the maximal pro-p comparison. D.32 then applies the three-cusp finite-cover rank argument to this exact subgroup and proves C=Fhat2. Thus every homomorphism C_p to full GT_0 covered by D.28 is trivial; in particular all odd-prime torsion is excluded.

The need for D.32's third-cusp hypothesis is demonstrated by an actual order-three automorphism. Let u be one in every prime coordinate except seven and a primitive cube root at seven. The substitution beta(x)=x^u, beta(y)=y^u has order three and a proper fixed subgroup, but the same Brown argument gives C_beta^(3) ≅ F2^(3). The missing third cusp is explicitly detected in the order-fourteen dihedral group: x=s, y=sr, and u=9 modulo14 give x^u y^u=r while (xy)^u=r^2, which are not conjugate. This is a proved obstruction to using the maximal pro-p quotient to identify the full fixed subgroup.

# D.31: finite groups in geometric completions

## Proved result

Every finite nonsolvable subgroup of the positive punctured-sphere geometric completion is abstractly A5. Its puncture action consists of at most one orbit of each exceptional size 12,20,30 and any number of free orbits of size60. In the extended sphere completion the nonsolvable abstract groups are A5 and A5×C2. In genera one and two, with arbitrary puncture number and orientation reversal, every finite subgroup is solvable.

The proof does not supply conjugacy of a completed A5 subgroup into the discrete sphere mapping class group or the full A5 centralizer equality. Those exact maps remain the open part of F.7.

## Completed maps checked

1. A finitely generated kernel and a good quotient give an exact completed extension. The proof works modulo each characteristic finite-index subgroup of the kernel, centralizes the resulting finite normal group, uses goodness to split the finite central extension over a finite-index subgroup, and takes the core of a complement. This directly verifies the induced topology on the original kernel.
2. Capping the boundary of a punctured disc gives the braid central extension of a sphere puncture stabilizer. The full twist maps to (n−1)(n−2) in braid abelianization, so its full Zhat topology is retained. Finite pullbacks have a central open Zhat, and transfer embeds each pullback into Zhat because the ambient completed braid group is torsion-free. The finite quotient is therefore cyclic.
3. The same transfer works with the central diagonal torus Zhat². Total strand homology sends the diagonal translation subgroup to n times Z² and proves its full induced topology. A finite subgroup of the quotient braid completion is consequently abelian.
4. The genus-two puncture-forgetting kernel is the torsion-free completion of a surface braid group; finite groups inject after forgetting. The hyperelliptic quotient has finite kernel C2, detected on homology modulo3, and quotient the sphere group with six punctures. The sphere orbit bound excludes nonsolvable finite images there.
5. The genus-one forgetting kernel is the completed quotient of the torus braid group by diagonal Z². Its finite subgroups are abelian, and the quotient is the completed SL2(Z), whose finite subgroups are cyclic by D.8. Orientation reversal adds an extension of index at most2.

The small sphere cases n=0,1,2 are explicit: positive groups 1,1,C2 and extended groups of order at most4. The branch-point solvability lemma is stated for a nonempty set of 1≤b≤3 points. The pure completed sphere group is torsion-free by its ordered-configuration description, proving faithfulness of each finite puncture-permutation action.

## Exact finite-group reduction

Prime-power comparison gives cyclic odd Sylow subgroups and cyclic or dihedral Sylow2 groups. It also retains the geometric normalizer image in Aut(Cp), which is contained in the two exponents ±1. A nontrivial finite solvable normal subgroup has a characteristic normal p-subgroup. The quotient of its completed normalizer preserves the two or three branch points of the geometric p-group cover; a finite group there has cyclic pointwise branch stabilizer and solvable permutation image. This forces the original finite group to be solvable, so a nonsolvable finite group has trivial solvable radical.

The original Gorenstein–Walter 1962 Theorem I is sufficient. Its extra hypothesis is proved: for a central Sylow2 involution z, the quotient of C_G(z) by z preserves the two branch points. Its pointwise kernel is cyclic, and the corresponding preimage is abelian of index at most2. Its odd part is a cyclic normal 2-complement. The theorem then gives PSL2(q), PGL2(q), A7 or a 2-group modulo an odd normal subgroup. A least-prime transfer argument proves solvability of groups with all Sylows cyclic, so the odd normal subgroup is trivial. C3² excludes A7, the additive defining-field subgroup forces q prime, and the diagonal normalizer action leaves only PSL2(5). The exact isomorphism to A5 is conjugation on its five Sylow2 groups.

For the extended sphere group, conjugation on the positive A5 embeds an extension with trivial centralizer into Aut(A5)=S5. The group S5 has a C5 normalizer inducing all four automorphisms of C5, violating the completed ±1 bound. A nontrivial centralizer gives the direct product with a negative C2.

# D.35: exact involution-conjugator criterion

The TeX result gives a proved parametrization, not a claim that all its solution spaces are nonempty.

Let F=Fhat(x,y), let P be the full pure three-cusp group, and let delta invert x and y. D.34 supplies a normalized involution alpha=(-1,f) and a solution h0 in F' of f=h0^-1 alpha(h0).

## The exact remaining equation

All coboundary solutions are h=c h0 with c in the actual fixed subgroup C_F(alpha). This fixed subgroup lies in F' because alpha acts by -1 on full abelianization.

The normalized endomorphism beta(x)=x^mu, beta(y)=h y^mu h^-1 intertwines alpha beta=beta delta exactly when h^-1 alpha(h)=f. Its third-cusp requirement is

    x^mu h y^mu h^-1 = u (xy)^mu u^-1.

The closed image is generated by two elements with independent ambient mod-two characters, hence has first cohomology of dimension exactly two. The third-cusp equation puts all three full cusp Z_2 parts in this image. D.32 therefore forces the image to be F; the finitely generated profinite Hopfian property makes beta an automorphism. This closes the full-generation implication once that displayed relation is present.

The solution space modulo the explicit right action u -> u(xy)^a maps homeomorphically to the actual P-conjugator set. Thus no normalization or change of conjugacy group is implicit.

## Exact bridge from P-conjugacy to GT_0-conjugacy

The key auxiliary equality is C_{P^1}(delta)=1, where P^1 is the multiplier-one kernel. A normalized pair (1,k) commuting with delta has delta(k)=k. The explicit isomorphism

    F semidirect_delta C2 = C2 coproduct C2 coproduct C2

sends the three factors to s, xs, ys. Full-profinite free-factor malnormality makes the centralizer of s exactly C2, so C_F(delta)=1 and k=1.

Harbater-Schneps Propositions 3-4 identify GT_0 exactly with C_P(S3), with theta(x)=y, theta(y)=x and omega(x)=y, omega(y)=(xy)^-1 as the specified outer S3 generators. For alpha in GT_0 and a P-conjugator beta, the element r=beta^-1 sigma beta sigma^-1 lies in P^1 and centralizes delta. Hence r=1 for every sigma in S3. Therefore beta belongs to GT_0. The Harbater-Schneps equations I and II follow, rather than being suppressed.

## Finite criterion

For every open characteristic N, take Q=F/N and m=exp(Q). Enumerate triples (a,b,v) in (Z/m)^units x Q' x Q satisfying the two displayed equations modulo N. All such finite sets are nonempty exactly when the full conjugator set is nonempty. The proof uses a common characteristic refinement for each finite collection of conditions and compactness of Zhat^units x F' x F. The map F' -> Q' is onto; unit residues lift by CRT.

The program code/pure_involution_conjugator.py ran successfully. In A5 set x=(1 2 3), y=(3 4 5), and put d=[x,y] and

    w = y d^-1 y^-1 x^-1 d^-1 x.

The program verifies that x,y generate all 60 elements, while w=(1 4 3 2 5) and wyw^-1=x. Therefore the endomorphism x -> x, y -> wyw^-1 has image of order 3 in this quotient, proving its full profinite image is proper. Its identity abelianization makes its induced endomorphism an automorphism on every maximal pro-p quotient, by Frattini. The witness is not claimed to satisfy the full involution coboundary equation. It demonstrates the exact failure of the generation inference that D.35 repairs using the third cusp.

# Finite centralizer source audit and the A5 finite image

## Exact source step

The complete supplied TeX of Boggi, arXiv:2408.12486v2, was inspected at Proposition `centgood` (published Proposition2.4), its use in the proof of `Gcentconf` in the general case of TheoremA, and the proof of TheoremC. The complete supplied TeX of Boggi–Zalesskii, arXiv:2406.08639v2, was inspected at Theorem5.1(iii), the prime-subgroup theorem, and the centralizer/normalizer criteria in Section2. The primary arXiv HTML for the latter was also opened.

Both all-finite centralizer proofs display the final equality

    intersection of closures C_G(x_i) = closure of intersection C_G(x_i).

The preceding prime-order or torsion-element centralizer results establish the expression on the left as the ambient centralizer. They do not, by themselves, establish the final equality. No counterexample to the stated source theorem is claimed. The audit records an absent justification and the exact residual finite-refinement problem.

The general branch-removal proof of Boggi's centralizer congruence theorem uses Proposition2.4 as well, so using that theorem for an arbitrary nonsolvable subgroup would not independently repair the centralizer equality. For a p-group, the needed Proposition2.4 application follows directly from Boggi–Zalesskii TheoremA, without any closure-intersection step. This supplies a sound prime-power congruence/topology input.

## Completed solvable proof

The TeX draft proves the solvable result by induction using a characteristic p-primary subgroup of the last nonzero derived term. The prime-power normalizer has its full profinite topology by the preceding checked case. Its quotient by that p-subgroup is a finite-index subgroup of the mapping class group of the decorated quotient surface, again of genus at most two. The normalizer of the remaining solvable quotient is handled by induction and pulled back. The finite-kernel diagram proves the induced topology statement at the same time. Finally, the conjugation homomorphism to the finite group Aut(J) has an open kernel; density of the discrete normalizer in the completed normalizer proves density of the discrete centralizer in that kernel. This proof does not invoke an all-finite centralizer result at an earlier stage.

## New proved A5 comparison at the puncture-permutation level

The puncture set consists of some exceptional orbits of sizes12,20,30 and m free orbits of size60. The ambient completed centralizer and the discrete centralizer have the same permutation image: every exceptional puncture is fixed individually, and the free orbits carry the entire wreath product A5^m semidirect S_m.

For order-three and order-five stabilizers, a positive commuting homeomorphism fixes the two poles because their oriented local rotation numbers differ. Prime-power centralizer comparison transfers this finite permutation constraint to the completion. For an order-two stabilizer, place it in A4. The positive actual centralizer of A4 fixes its branch points and is isotopic to the identity through commuting maps: descend to the quotient sphere with three branch points, isotope there, and lift; the terminal deck transformation belongs to Z(A4)=1. Therefore it fixes all six order-two ramification points. The proved solvable comparison transfers that constraint to the completion. These constraints eliminate the nonidentity element of each two-element transitive permutation commutant.

The TeX note proves its cohomology class is nonzero by restricting a proposed coboundary to the two commuting factors. It also proves `H1(A5 x A5, V tensor V) = 0`. No non-splitting claim is inferred solely from finite samples of the cocycle identity.

The simultaneous refinement uses the six ordered pairs

`(3,13), (5,15), (6,8), (7,8), (11,13), (14,15)`

over the support `{3,5,6,7,8,11,13,14,15}`. Thus the base is exactly `A5^9`, the noncentral kernel is the direct sum of six 9-dimensional tensor modules, and the group has order `60^9 * 5^54`. The six nonzero extension components make the kernel Frattini. Consequently every lift of the specified generating pair generates the full extension.

## Simultaneous systems and counts

The first affine system imposes the exact word maps `theta(X)=Y`, `theta(Y)=X`, `omega(X)=Y`, and `omega(Y)=(XY)^-1`. After quotienting by simultaneous inner conjugation by the module, the solution space has dimension 9 over F5.

For each base tuple `t`, the second system imposes

`T^2 = 1`, `T X T^-1 = X^-1`, and `omega(T) = Y^-1 theta(T)`.

Every one of the 300 systems has dimension 6. Its projection to the 9-dimensional family of symmetry-invariant kernels has dimension 3. Therefore each base tuple has exactly 125 compatible kernels and 125 involutions on each kernel, giving 15,625 pairs per tuple and 4,687,500 pairs altogether. Exactly half lie over the base tuples inside the restricted D.38 conjugacy model, and half lie over the base tuples outside it.

Direct group multiplication on one solution for each of the 300 tuples verifies the symmetry word maps, the involution norm, the inversion equation, and both Harbater–Schneps relations. The linear equations and the exact cancellation proof establish these identities on the whole affine solution sets.

## Scope and remaining obstruction

The extension family is a necessary finite test for an actual GT0 involution: its induced action and the geometric S3 act affinely on the 54-dimensional family of epimorphism kernels, and averaging over the group of order 12 in characteristic 5 supplies a common fixed kernel. The note spells out the target automorphism and kernel identifications used in this argument.

The calculation supplies no compatible inverse system of lifts. It also supplies no solution of the full third-cusp conjugator equation in D.35. # Audit note: the exact remaining centralizer restriction

This note records a limitation of the currently proved centralizer constraints. It does **not** construct an actual nonstandard pants involution or realize the comparison subgroup below as its fixed subgroup.

Let `alpha = (-1,f)` be an actual GT0 involution, `E = F ⋊ <s>`, and `C = C_F(s)`, with `F = Fhat(x,y)`. D.34 proves `H1(C,F2)=0`. Since alpha acts by -1 on the torsion-free abelianization `Zhat^2`, every fixed element has zero abelianization, so `C <= F′`.

D.44 supplies an involution `h tau` commuting with s, where tau acts by the geometric swap `theta(x)=y`, `theta(y)=x`, and `h=k^-1 theta(k)`. Its conjugation action on F is exactly

`sigma = Inn(h) theta = Inn(k^-1) theta Inn(k)`.

Thus sigma preserves C and has no nonidentity fixed point on C: its full fixed subgroup on F is conjugate to `C_F(theta)=1`, by the explicitly identified free product `F ⋊ <tau> = C2 ∐ Zhat`.

These individual properties permit nontrivial closed comparison subgroups even after imposing any specified finite collection of quotient kernels. To see this directly, let `pi_j:F -> Q_j` be that collection, let m be a positive common multiple of the exponents of the finite groups Q_j, fix an odd prime p, and put

`c=[x,y]`, `C0 = <c^(m e_p)>`,

where `e_p` is 1 in the p-coordinate of Zhat and 0 in every other coordinate.

The map `Zhat -> F`, `a -> c^a`, is injective. For every prime l and n>=1, map x and y to the two standard generators in the group of upper unitriangular 3-by-3 matrices over `Z/l^n`. Their commutator has central coordinate 1 and exact order `l^n`. Hence `c^a=1` forces `a=0 mod l^n` for every l,n, and therefore a=0 in Zhat. Restricting this injection to `m e_p Z_p` proves that C0 is isomorphic to Z_p and is nontrivial.

All remaining comparisons are exact:

- `C0 <= F′`, since c is a commutator.
- `pi_j(C0)=1` for every j, since m annihilates every cyclic subgroup in Q_j.
- `H1(C0,F2)=Hom_cont(Z_p,C2)=0`, since p is odd.
- `theta(c)=c^-1`, so theta preserves C0 and acts by inversion.
- Its only fixed element on C0 is the identity, since multiplication by 2 is injective on Z_p.

For the actual conjugate swap sigma, the comparison subgroup is `k^-1 C0 k`. It remains inside F′ and all the selected normal kernels, and sigma acts on it by inversion with no nonidentity fixed point.

This proves only that the listed subgroup properties do not force triviality. **No assertion is made that C0 or its conjugate equals `C_F(s)` for any pants involution.** The actual fixed-subgroup realization, together with the three full cusp normalizers, imposes conditions not discharged by this comparison.

## Exact coherent-triple map

For a D.35 solution `(mu,h,u)`, the three elements

`r0=s`, `r1=x^mu s`, `r2=s h y^mu h^-1`

are involutions. Their products are respectively

`r1 r0=x^mu`, `r0 r2=h y^mu h^-1`, and `r1 r2=u(xy)^mu u^-1`.

The product subgroup in F is generated by two elements and contains conjugates of all three full cusp Z2 subgroups. D.32 makes it all of F. Consequently the homomorphism from `C2 ∐ C2 ∐ C2` sending its three named generators to r0,r1,r2 is surjective onto E. It preserves the parity maps to C2, and its restriction between their rank-two free profinite kernels is surjective; the Hopfian property of Fhat2 makes that restriction injective. Its entire kernel is contained in that parity kernel, so the original homomorphism is an isomorphism.

The incidence triangle proved in D.34 supplies the three conjugacy classes and their cusp incidences. The displayed equality for `r1 r2` is exactly the third-cusp equation of D.35. Its existence has not been obtained from the incidence triangle alone in this audit.

1. EXACT COMPLETED RESULT

Use the original negative basis X1,...,X7 and the positive basis
Yi=B_+(Xi), with the exact based isomorphism and inverse of F.23.13.

2. ACTUAL SCALAR FIELDS AND INVERSE COEFFICIENT MAPS

The character is (1,s,t,u,v,w,z), h=s*t*u*v*w*z.
The actual normal-generation map of F.21/F.22 gives

  C=chi(K)=chi(R)=<u,v,w,z>,

3. ACTUAL PRINCIPAL QUOTIENT AND ITS COMPLETE INVERSE MAPS

Every seven-tuple of generator cocycle values gives a finite

2. Compact-open topology comparison

The note proves the needed comparison on every surface without boundary
instead of identifying the two topologies without their maps.
For a compact-open continuous family f_a, fix (a_*,y_*) and a small
closed coordinate disk D0 around f_{a_*}^{-1}(y_*). Choose a connected
target disk V whose compact closure lies inside f_{a_*}(int D0).
Nearby f_a have their boundary images disjoint from Vbar and send the
chosen interior point into V. The two relatively open sets

    V intersect f_a(int D0),      V minus f_a(D0)

partition V; the first is nonempty. Connectedness makes the second empty.
Thus f_a^{-1}(V) is contained in D0. This proves joint inverse continuity
for arbitrary parameter spaces a. Local compactness and the compact-open
exponential law make inversion continuous as a map of function spaces.
The two topology comparisons are the identity map forgetting inverse
coordinates and its identity inverse, continuous by that inversion map.
Joint evaluation also proves composition continuity.

The actual quotient is separable because its open covering map sends a
countable basis to a countable basis. The C82 triangulation is subdivided
at p. It is boundaryless, so Yagasaki's proper-embedding requirements
f(X intersect boundary M) subset boundary M and f(X intersect int M)
subset int M are automatic for the embeddings used here.

4. Explicit finite parametric extension, including both maps

The construction starts with a specified continuous embedding homotopy

All local extension charts are chosen with this same U.

The note gives actual bump functions beta_i=(delta/4-d(u,v_i))_+ and
alpha_i=beta_i/sum beta_j. Their supports lie in U_i=B(v_i,delta/3).
The diameter of bar U_i times a time strip is at most 2delta/3, so the
whole closed set lies in one extension-chart preimage.

On a strip [a,b] the intermediate times are

Their ordered chart increments are the actual homeomorphisms

Their inverses reverse these two factors. On the open overlap where
alpha_i=0, the two arguments coincide, so the map is exactly the identity.
The chart formula and the outside-support identity paste continuously
on the two specified open sets covering P. Both map and inverse paste.
The actual equation Gamma_i e_{u,t_{i-1}}=e_{u,t_i} follows from the
two local extension equations at the same reference embedding.

The ordered product Gamma_m ... Gamma_1 g_{u,a} is g_{u,t}; its inverse

strip every Gamma is identity, so adjoining strips agree exactly.
Induction proves g|X=e. All factors fix K and M minus U. At u0 both
embedding arguments are inclusion, even when a chart's reference is
another embedding, so g_{u0,t}=identity.

This construction gives a finite product with an explicit inverse.
It does not rely on an unstated bundle-lifting choice, a contractible
parameter space P, or a uniform bound on the number of future stages.

## The actual negative transposition and all original cusp transporters

THE ACTUAL GT0 NEGATIVE TRANSPOSITION: FULL CENTRALIZER AND TRANSPORTERS
=====================================================================
Separate unnumbered proved continuation. No frozen source is modified.
The original D74.40 solution set remains the one defined using the
same unique h. No realization or nonemptiness conclusion is asserted.

1. The specified actual automorphism and its extension
-----------------------------------------------------
Retain the actual nonidentity involution alpha in GT0, its original
F=Fhat(x,y), z=(xy)^(-1), and its unique h in F' from D74. Put
  Y=h y h^(-1),  psi=Inn(h) theta,  J=alpha psi,
where theta(x)=y, theta(y)=x. The original identities give
  psi^2=1,  alpha psi=psi alpha,  J^2=1,
  psi(x)=Y, psi(Y)=x, J(x)=Y^(-1), J(Y)=x^(-1).             (1)
For the commutation, theta alpha theta=Inn(f)alpha and
alpha(h)=hf give
  psi alpha=Inn(hf)alpha theta=alpha psi.
The square of psi uses h theta(h)=1. All these are actual
automorphisms of the original F. On its named abelian basis,
  alpha_*=-I,  psi_*=[[0,1],[1,0]],
  J_*=[[0,-1],[-1,0]].                                   (2)
Thus J's outer class exchanges the original x and y cusps, fixes
the z cusp, and has the full global multiplier -1. This last value
uses the original alpha multiplier, not only its 2-adic coordinate.

Form the specified extension
  E_J=F semidirect_J <j | j^2=1>,
  u:E_J->C2, u(j)=1.                                     (3)
Let L_x=<x>, L_y=<y>, L_z=<z>, with full procyclic closures.
There is an actual a_z in F with J(z)=a_z z^(-1)a_z^(-1).
Set v=a_z^(-1)j. Then v normalizes L_z and inverts z.
Its square is in F and centralizes z, so v^2=z^a for one full
exponent a, by A.7. Conjugating this equation by v gives a=-a;
the full Zhat has no element killed by two, so v^2=1.

The two actual boundary-orbit stabilizers are
  D_x=N_(E_J)(L_x)=L_x,
  D_z=N_(E_J)(L_z)=L_z semidirect_-1 <v>.                 (4)
For D_x, an odd-parity normalizer would preserve the x cusp class,
contrary to the stated exchange of distinct x and y classes.
Its even-parity normalizer is L_x by A.7. For D_z the kernel in F
is L_z and v supplies the other coset. The inverse continuous maps
for the second equality in (4) are
  (a,epsilon)->z^a v^epsilon,
  d->(a,u(d)), where d v^(-u(d))=z^a.                    (5)

2. One full section class, without identifying its fixed subgroup
----------------------------------------------------------------
On H^1(F,F2), (2) is the nontrivial two-dimensional regular C2
module. Its positive C2 cohomology is zero. The split extension
(3) and its two-row Hochschild--Serre sequence consequently give
  dim H^n(E_J,F2)=1 for n>=3.                            (6)
This is the literal regular-module computation used in D37, now
with the original x,y labels; no relabelling of the cusps is needed.
Every nontrivial finite subgroup injects into E_J/F=C2, since F
is torsion-free. The full Brown restriction theorem used in D37
therefore applies. Each section class contributes at least one
dimension to (6), and the section v already exists. Thus there is
exactly one E_J-conjugacy class of nontrivial sections.

Conjugacy is also by F: for a section S, E_J=F S, and its S factor
centralizes itself. Hence both v and zv, and also j, are F-conjugate.
At this point (6) supplies only zero mod-two H1 for their fixed
subgroup. The full assertion below will use finite permutation
coefficients and the original boundary maps.

3. Exact three-cusp restriction of a two-orbit boundary module
--------------------------------------------------------------
Choose b in F so that
  v x v^(-1)=b y^(-1)b^(-1).
This is permitted by the original multiplier -1 and cusp exchange.
With k=F2 form
  P_boundary=k[[E_J/D_x]] direct_sum k[[E_J/D_z]],
  0->Delta->P_boundary--augmentation-->k->0.              (7)
There are explicit F-equivariant homeomorphisms of the three
original coset spaces onto the indicated parity orbits:
  F/L_x -> E_J/D_x,     aL_x -> aD_x,
  F/L_y -> E_J/D_x,     aL_y -> a b^(-1)vD_x,
  F/L_z -> E_J/D_z,     aL_z -> aD_z.                     (8)
The first two images are disjoint and together exhaust E_J/D_x.
The stabilizer of b^(-1)vD_x in F is L_y, by the displayed equation
for v x v^(-1); the other stabilizers are L_x and L_z. These facts
prove bijectivity. Compactness and the Hausdorff coset topologies
give inverse continuity. Thus Delta restricted to F is exactly
the original full three-cusp augmentation module.

For completeness, left multiplication by v in these coordinates is
  aL_x -> (v a v^(-1)b)L_y,
  aL_y -> (v a b^(-1)v^(-1))L_x,

Together with ordinary left F multiplication these are the transported

4. The exact finite-coefficient half-rank calculation
----------------------------------------------------
For a finite continuous k[E_J]-module M define
  H_M=Hom_(k,continuous)(Delta,M),
  (e phi)(d)=e phi(e^(-1)d).
It is the actual discrete coefficient module used for the relative
groups R^n(E_J,M)=H^(n-1)(E_J,H_M), n>=1. Applying continuous Hom
to (7) and Shapiro gives the actual subgroup-restriction sequence
  ... -> H^n(E_J,M)
      -> H^n(D_x,M) direct_sum H^n(D_z,M)
      -> R^(n+1)(E_J,M) -> H^(n+1)(E_J,M) -> ... .         (10)
All compact k-vector spaces in (7) are projective over k, so its
underlying vector-space split gives the required exact Hom sequence.

The coefficient evaluation pairing is
  M tensor H_(M^vee) -> H_k,
       m tensor phi -> [d->phi(d)(m)].                   (11)
It is E_J-equivariant. Through the explicit maps (8), the surface
pair is the original completed pair of pants with x,y,z. Its perfect
absolute-relative cup pairings give, for
  A=H^0(F,M), B=H^1(F,M),
the equivariant identifications
  H^0(F,H_(M^vee))=B^vee,
  H^1(F,H_(M^vee))=A^vee.                               (12)
These are precisely the cup comparisons of D74.13--17 applied to
the module (7) via (8). The target orientation group is one-dimensional
over F2, so its E_J/F action is trivial even though (9) exchanges two
boundary summands. Equivariance follows from (11), not from a
geometric realization of J.

The ordinary Hochschild--Serre sequences for M and H_(M^vee) have
only rows zero and one. In positive quotient columns their entries
are, respectively, Abar,Bbar and (B^vee)bar,(A^vee)bar, where
  Vbar=ker(1+sigma)/im(1+sigma).
The evaluation pairing between Vbar and (V^vee)bar is perfect;
the annihilator identities are those explicitly proved in D74.19.
Multiplication by the actual quotient class u is the identity in
these cyclic positive-column coordinates.

The filtered cup product from (11) has the same derivation identity
as D74.23. The product of an absolute fiber-row-one element with a
shifted-relative fiber-row-one element is zero in
H^2(F,H_k). Thus the two d2 maps are transposes for the perfect
positive-column pairings, and have the same rank. There are no later
differentials. Consequently, for self-dual M, the stable absolute
and relative dimensions are equal. Multiplication by u identifies
successive sufficiently high groups, as in D74.24--25.

The procyclic D_x has cd_2=1, so its terms in (10) vanish in these
high degrees. Its u-localization is zero; no positive-periodicity
assertion for a nonzero D_x group is needed. D_z has the usual

  B_M=H^bullet(D_z,M)[u^(-1)]_0,
  R_M=R^bullet(E_J,M)[u^(-1)]_0.
They are finite-dimensional and (10) becomes the exact cyclic

Suppose c in C is nonidentity. Choose an open normal N of E_J
contained in F with c not in N. Put W=E_J/N, Q=F/N, and Sbar=SN/N.
The actual finite permutation coefficient
  M=k[W/Sbar]
has its invariant perfect basis pairing, and therefore qualifies

The coset Sbar is fixed. The nontrivial element cbar in Q centralizes

On the other hand every class in the restriction image of r_S is

is exactly c on M. Naturality of restriction and the same bar prism
prove this assertion before and after localization. The moved basis
class contradicts surjectivity of r_S. Hence
  C_F(v)=1, N_(E_J)(S)=S, and C_F(J)=1.                  (16)
The last equality uses the original j section and its F-conjugacy
to v from Section 2. It is a full original-group equality.

Every involution in E_J now has its own C2 as full centralizer.
The nonidentity involution set is closed: it is the intersection
of {g:g^2=1} with the clopen set E_J\F. The actual F is an open
projective subgroup of index two. These verify the same hypotheses
of Haran Proposition 2.2 used in D74, so E_J is real projective.
This is its stated weak finite embedding-problem property, with
no assertion that solutions are onto.

6. Unique original cusp transporters and their full coordinates
----------------------------------------------------------------
There is now a unique g in F with
  g v g^(-1)=zv, equivalently [g,v]=z.                   (17)
Existence is Section 2 and uniqueness is C_F(v)=1. On the named
full abelian basis write [g]=(a,b). Since v induces the same matrix
as J in (2), (17) gives
  (I-J_*)[g]=[z]=(-1,-1), hence a+b=-1.                 (18)
In particular the exact character
  chi:F->Zhat,  chi(x)=chi(y)=-1
satisfies chi(g)=1. It is not asserted that g belongs to a free
basis or that a-b is a full unit.

This character also gives the exact centralizer coordinates of g:
  C_F(g)=(C_F(g) cap ker chi) x <g>.
The maps send c to (c g^(-chi(c)),g^chi(c)) and multiply in the
other direction. The factor <g> is the full Zhat, since chi splits
its exponent map. A nontrivial first factor has a nontrivial pro-p
Sylow subgroup for some p. Because F is torsion-free, any nontrivial
element in that subgroup generates a closed Z_p. Its direct product
with the central Z_p in <g> is a closed Z_p x Z_p inside F, which
has nonzero H2 over F_p, contrary to cd_p(F)=1. Thus that first
factor is trivial. A normalizer of <g> acts by a unit exponent;
applying chi forces that exponent to be one. Therefore
  C_F(g)=N_F(<g>)=<g> isomorphic to Zhat.                (19)
These are the same explicit primitive-character coordinates used
in the accepted original-tau cusp note, now for this actual g.

For every nu in Zhat, let epsilon be its residue in {0,1} modulo
two. The entire original transporter set is the singleton
  {a in F:a v a^(-1)=z^nu v}
       ={z^((nu-epsilon)/2) g^epsilon}.                (20)
The half-exponent uses the continuous inverse of multiplication by
two on 2 Zhat. Direct conjugation by the displayed element gives
z^(nu-epsilon+epsilon)v; uniqueness again uses (16). The dependence
on nu is continuous on its two clopen parity pieces. Its inverse
on its compact image is the specified character chi,
because chi(z) = 2 and chi(g)=1 give chi(a)=nu.

In particular for every full unit mu the exact transporter is
  a_mu=z^((mu-1)/2)g.                                    (21)
The group, the original cusp z, the section v, and every exponent
in (17)--(21) are retained. These formulas do not assert that
g and J(g) generate F or align the other two original cusps.

7. Retained scope
------------------
The new conclusion is the full trivial fixed subgroup of the actual
negative transposition J in (1), together with its marked extension,
real-projectivity statement and unique original cusp transporters.
Its boundary calculation uses (7)--(9), with the paired x/y cusp
orbit kept through exact maps. The D74 two-row cup/transgression
proof, finite-coefficient Brown theorem and Haran characterization
are the already checked sources used here; no new literature
recognition theorem is imported.

The separate original norm branches still use the unique original h,
and T has not been proved nonempty. No additional local pro-p H_r
has been substituted for h. No numbered claim is assigned by this
note, and no free-product realization of E or E_J is concluded.


## The actual marked V4 extension and exact cusp endomorphism

THE ACTUAL MARKED V4 EXTENSION AND ITS CUSP-FIXING ENDOMORPHISM
=============================================================
Separate unnumbered proved continuation; no numbered claim is assigned.
It uses the frozen actual-J centralizer calculation. No earlier file
is changed. All maps below retain the original alpha, h, x, y and z.
The original D74.40 norm set T remains unresolved.

1. The actual extension and its positive subgroup
-------------------------------------------------
Use the exact D44 extension
  E=F semidirect_alpha <s>,
  G=E semidirect_Theta <tau>,
  Theta|_F=theta, Theta(s)=fs, theta(x)=y, theta(y)=x.
Here s^2=tau^2=1. Write the quotient G/F as V4 with coordinates
  s -> (1,0), tau -> (0,1).
The original h satisfies alpha(h)=hf and h theta(h)=1. Thus
  Y=h y h^(-1), t=h tau, j=st=ts,
  Q0=<s,t> is a specified subgroup isomorphic to V4.
Conjugation by t on F is psi=Inn(h)theta; conjugation by j is
the original J=alpha psi in the frozen negative-transposition note.
The quotient images of t and j are (0,1) and (1,1).

Let G_+ be the inverse image of <(0,1)>. It is the same actual
subgroup both in F semidirect_theta <tau> and F semidirect_psi <t>.
The full coproduct maps
  C2(T) amalg Zhat(P) -> G_+,  T->tau, P->p=x tau,
have the explicit inverse
  x->PT, y->TP, tau->T.
The inverse respects tau x tau=y and tau y tau=x; both composites
fix the displayed generators. Thus the identification is full,
continuous, and has the indicated continuous inverse. In particular
  p^2=xy=z^(-1), x=p tau, y=tau p.                       (1)
The original F is the kernel of G_+->C2 sending both p and tau to 1.
The subgroup <p> is a full Zhat: the map G_+->Zhat sending p to 1
and tau to 0 splits its exponent map.

2. The exact original z-cusp normalizer in G
--------------------------------------------
Retain the normalized original z-reflection from the accepted GT0
note:
  u1=omega^2(h) in F', r=u1 x s u1^(-1),
  r^2=1, r z r=z^(-1), rF=(1,0).                       (2)
The outer multiplier on G/F is (-1) to the first coordinate.
Therefore the image of C_G(z) in G/F lies in <(0,1)>: an odd first
coordinate would make z F-conjugate to z^(-1). Their original
abelian vectors (-1,-1) and (1,1) are unequal. Its kernel
is C_F(z)=<z>, by A.7; p supplies the other coset. Using p^2=z^(-1),
  C_G(z)=<p>.
Every normalizer of <z> has one of the four quotient coordinates.
The elements p and r supply all four, and its kernel in F is <z>.
Moreover r p r belongs to C_G(z)=<p> and has square p^(-2).
Writing it p^a gives 2a=-2, hence a=-1 in the full Zhat. Consequently
  N_G(<z>)=<p> semidirect_-1 <r>, r p r=p^(-1).          (3)
The maps (a,e)->p^a r^e, and their inverse obtained from parity and
the p-exponent, give this equality as an isomorphism of profinite
groups. These maps in particular retain the original embedded L_z
as <p^2>; no extra choice of an abstract cusp is used.

Put
  v=p r.
Then v^2=1 and vF=(1,1), so v belongs to the actual negative-
transposition extension F<j>. The fixed-cusp relations are
  v z v=z^(-1), r v r=p^(-1)r=zv.                      (4)

3. The unique J transporter supplies an actual V4
------------------------------------------------
The frozen J calculation applies to v in the same actual extension:
all its sections are F-conjugate and C_F(v)=1. There is a unique
  g in F with g v g^(-1)=zv.
On the original abelian basis write [g]=(a,b). Its equation gives
  a+b=-1.                                              (5)
The exact character chi(x)=chi(y)=-1 has chi(g)=1, and the frozen
primitive-character proof gives C_F(g)=N_F(<g>)=<g>.

Define
  q=g^(-1)r.
Equations (4) and the g equation show that q centralizes v. Its
quotient coordinate is (1,0), so q^2 lies in F and centralizes v.
Since C_F(v)=1, q^2=1. Thus
  Q=<q,v> is a specified V4, and qv has coordinate (0,1). (6)
The quotient identifies Q with G/F, since the two nonzero coordinates
of q and v are independent.

The element q belongs to the original E and is F-conjugate to s.
To see the particular class without choosing representatives,
compute its F-component in the split coordinates E=F<s>.
Equation (2) has abelian F-component (1,0), because u1 is in F'.
Therefore q has abelian F-component
  (1-a,-b), whose coordinate sum is 2.
Conjugating an E-involution by an element of F changes this vector
by twice an integral profinite vector. D74's three full F-classes
are represented by s, xs and Ys, with mod-two vectors respectively
  (0,0), (1,0), (0,1).
Only the first has even coordinate sum. This proves that q is in
the class of s, and also proves
  a=1 modulo 2, b=0 modulo 2.                            (7)

Let w be the unique element of F with
  q=w s w^(-1).
Existence was just proved; uniqueness is the full C_F(s)=1.
The full C_G(s) equals Q0: its map to G/F is injective by C_F(s)=1,
and Q0 already supplies four distinct quotient elements. Since
v centralizes q and has coordinate (1,1), it follows exactly that
  v=w j w^(-1), t'=qv=w t w^(-1).                      (8)
In particular t' is an actual involution of G_+.

The involution h tau is conjugate to tau inside the already identified
C2 amalg Zhat=G_+: its torsion lies in a conjugate of the C2 factor.
The conjugator can be taken in F, because G_+=F<tau>. This is the
same full torsion-factor clause used in D44. Hence t' also is
F-conjugate to tau. No assertion about a generated subgroup follows
from this conjugacy alone.

4. A specified full coproduct map and its exact image
-----------------------------------------------------
Let
  P0=C2(R) amalg V4(Q,V),
where R,Q,V are involutions and QV=VQ. The actual elements in (2)
and (6) define a continuous homomorphism
  iota:P0->G, R->r, Q->q, V->v.                        (9)
Its image H is compact, hence closed, and is precisely <r,q,v>.
It contains p=vr. Both its image in G/F and its image in G/G_+
are the whole indicated finite quotients.

For the latter quotient put
  epsilon:P0->C2, epsilon(R)=epsilon(Q)=epsilon(V)=1,
  P_+=ker epsilon, P_0=VR, T_0=QV.
There is the following explicit full presentation, including inverse
maps:
  P0=(Zhat(P_0) amalg C2(T_0)) semidirect_sigma <R>,
  sigma(P_0)=P_0^(-1), sigma(T_0)=P_0^(-1)T_0 P_0.       (10)
The automorphism sigma squares to the identity. In the right-hand
group put V=P_0 R and Q=T_0 P_0 R; these are commuting involutions.
Conversely P_0=VR and T_0=QV recover its named generators in the
left-hand group, and conjugation by R has the displayed formulas.
Thus both full continuous homomorphisms are inverse on generators.
In particular P_+=Zhat(P_0) amalg C2(T_0) with the indicated basis.

The restriction iota_+ has exact images
  P_0->p, T_0->t'.                                     (11)
Moreover iota(P_+)=H cap G_+. To verify the reverse inclusion,
write any preimage of an element of H cap G_+ using (10). Its R
coordinate must be zero, since iota induces the identity on these
C2 quotients. Thus it already lies in P_+.

Use the explicit identification in Section 1 to identify P_+ with
G_+ by P_0->p and T_0->tau. The actual resulting endomorphism is
  eta:G_+->G_+, eta(p)=p, eta(tau)=t'=w h tau w^(-1).     (12)
This is a specified endomorphism arising from the original data and
the two proved unique transporters. In particular it is not an
arbitrary selection of a conjugate factor generator.

The image statement (11) gives the exact equivalences
  iota(P0)=G  <=> eta(G_+)=G_+ <=> eta is an automorphism. (13)
For the first equivalence, H contains r, whose image generates
G/G_+; thus H=G exactly when H cap G_+=G_+. For the second, a
surjective endomorphism of the finitely generated profinite G_+
is injective. Indeed for every
index n there are finitely many open subgroups of index n, by their
coset actions and finite generation. Surjective pullback is injective
on this finite set and hence permutes it. Thus for each open subgroup
U some positive iterate has eta^(-m)(U)=U; ker eta is contained in
that set U. Intersecting all open U makes ker eta trivial. Therefore
eta has its continuous inverse by compactness. At this point iota
also is an isomorphism: its kernel maps trivially to C2 and its
restriction to P_+ is identified with the injective eta. These are
equivalences for the specified maps; no side of (13) is asserted to
hold for a remaining actual nonstandard input.

5. The original F map, its cusp product and its exact determinant
----------------------------------------------------------------
The quotient G_+->C2 defining F sends t' to 1, since t' is conjugate
to tau, and sends p to 1. Thus eta preserves this quotient and F.
Using t'=qv=g^(-1)rv=g^(-1)p^(-1), (1) gives
  eta_F(x)=p g^(-1)p^(-1), eta_F(y)=g^(-1),
  eta_F(xy)=p t' t' p=p^2=xy,
  eta_F(z)=z.                                          (14)
There is no replacement of the original z generator in these maps.

Conjugation by p=x tau on F has original abelian matrix swapping
x and y. Therefore the exact abelian matrix of eta_F is
  [[-b,-a],[-a,-b]], det(eta_F,ab)=a-b,                 (15)
where a+b=-1. Equation (7) makes a-b odd at the prime 2. It does
not establish that a-b is a full unit. The endomorphism eta induces
the identity on the full G_+ abelianization Zhat(p) direct_sum C2(tau),
because t' is conjugate to tau; this latter statement alone supplies
no further determinant equality on the index-two subgroup F.

For completeness, eta_F(F)=eta(G_+) cap F, by the same quotient
coordinate argument as for (11). Both eta(G_+) and G_+ map onto
G_+/F. Consequently full surjectivity of eta_F is equivalent to
that of eta. No full surjectivity is obtained from (15).

There is also an exact automorphism-intertwining equation.
In (10), conjugation by Q=T_0P_0R fixes T_0 and sends P_0 to
T_0 P_0^(-1) T_0. Hence it inverts the two original-domain generators
  x_0=P_0T_0, y_0=T_0P_0
of the kernel of P_+->C2 sending P_0,T_0 to 1. The full inverse
maps of Section 1, with these symbol names, identify that kernel
with Fhat(x_0,y_0); it has index four in P0. Transporting (9) gives
  Inn(q) eta_F = eta_F delta,
where delta(x)=x^(-1), delta(y)=y^(-1).
Since q=w s w^(-1), the specified continuous homomorphism
  beta=Inn(w^(-1)) eta_F:F->F
satisfies
  alpha beta=beta delta, psi beta=beta theta,
  beta(z)=w^(-1)z w.                                   (16)
For the second equivariance, extend the formula for beta to G_+.
It sends tau to w^(-1)t'w=t, so conjugation by tau in the source
is carried to conjugation by t in the target. Restriction to F is
exactly the stated psi/theta identity.
Its two other original cusp images are exactly those in (14)
conjugated by w^(-1); no unit-power alignment with x and y has
been proved. Thus (16) is not supplied as a solution of D74.40.

6. Exact change of the original reflection
------------------------------------------
For any d in the full Zhat, replace r by
  r_d=z^d r z^(-d).
Keep the same p and put v_d=p r_d. Since p commutes with z,
  v_d=z^d v z^(-d), g_d=z^d g z^(-d),
  q_d=z^d q z^(-d), w_d=z^d w, t'_d=z^d t' z^(-d).      (17)
The g_d formula follows by conjugating the entire marked
g v g^(-1)=zv equation; the uniqueness C_F(v_d)=1 proves it
is the conjugator selected by the new construction. The q_d
formula follows from its definition. The w_d formula solves
the new s-conjugacy equation and is unique by C_F(s)=1.
The remaining formulas are then direct products.

Consequently the resulting maps have the exact comparison
  eta_d=Inn(z^d) eta on G_+,
  beta_d=beta on F.                                    (18)
For eta_d, check both p and tau; conjugation by z^d fixes p.
For beta_d, substitute w_d=z^d w into its definition. The
original abelian pair (a,b), and hence its difference a-b,
is unchanged. This keeps the entire same-section-class
reflection choice through actual homomorphisms.

7. Direct standard-input check and retained target
--------------------------------------------------
For the original standard input alpha=delta, f=h=1, one has
  t=tau, r=xs, p=x tau, j=s tau, v=xy j=z^(-1)j.
The displayed unique equations are solved by
  g=x^(-1), q=x^2s, w=x, t'=x tau x^(-1)=p tau p^(-1).
Direct substitution verifies every equation. Thus eta=Inn(p) on
G_+, eta_F(x)=x y x^(-1), eta_F(y)=x, and beta=theta on F.
In this input a=-1,b=0 and the determinant in (15) is -1.
This check uses the actual standard input, not an assignment of a
finite coordinate to any nonstandard original h.

For a remaining input, the unresolved target in this note is the
image of the actual eta (12), followed by the two original cusp

image/alignments nor nonemptiness of the original norm set T has
