## Actual full norm branches and the original-to-local coefficient image

ACTUAL CYCLIC NORM BRANCHES AND THE ODD-PRIME COEFFICIENT MAP
==========================================================
Unnumbered proved continuation, retaining the original GT0 involution.
No previously frozen note, producer, output, or review is changed.
The exact original full solution set T remains unproved nonempty.

1. The original word as a cube in a specified full free product
--------------------------------------------------------------
Retain F=Fhat(x,y), z=(xy)^(-1), the actual unique h of D74, and
omega(x)=y, omega(y)=z. Put
  L=F semidirect_omega <eta | eta^3=1>,  b=x eta.
There are explicit inverse continuous homomorphisms
  C3(A) amalg C3(B) -> L,       A->eta, B->x eta,
  L -> C3(A) amalg C3(B),
        x->B A^(-1), y->A B A^(-2), eta->A.                 (1)
Indeed (x eta)^3=xyz=1. In the reverse direction z maps to A^2 B,
and conjugation by A sends the displayed x-image to the y-image and
the y-image to the z-image. The two composites fix every named
generator, proving the isomorphism. The original F is the kernel
of the displayed quotient L->C3 sending both A and B to 1 modulo 3.

Let K={k in Zhat:2k+1 belongs to Zhat^times}, and retain
  D(k)=x^k omega^2(h)^(-1) z^k omega(h)^(-1) y^k h^(-1).
For the actual continuous curve
  a:K->L,       a(k)=h y^(-k) eta,
direct multiplication gives
  a(k)^3=h y^(-k) omega(h) z^(-k) omega^2(h) x^(-k)
        =D(k)^(-1).                                       (2)
Its image under L->C3 is the nonzero element 1. Thus D(k)=1 is
exactly the assertion that this specified a(k) has order three.
The parameter map k->mu=2k+1 is the same homeomorphism to the full
unit group used in the frozen transporter note.

The two full free factors in (1) have trivial mutual conjugate
intersections and are malnormal. The full-profinite statement of
Herfort--Zalesskii Theorem 5 supplies that property. Every nontrivial
finite subgroup of L is conjugate into one of the two factors, by
the unnumbered Corollary on printed page 598 of Scheiderer's Appendix
to Lochak--Schneps. Both source clauses and their exact read scope
are retained in Section 7 below.

In particular an order-three a(k) is conjugate to eta or b. The
other nonidentity powers are excluded by the given quotient to C3.
The conjugator can always be chosen in the original F: replace an
arbitrary conjugator g by g eta^(-j), or by g b^(-j), where j is
its image in L/F and the factor generator is the one being
conjugated. These changes preserve the conjugated element and put
the conjugator in F. The F-conjugator is unique, because
  C_F(eta)=C_F(b)=1:                                      (3)
malnormality puts a centralizer inside its order-three factor,
whose intersection with F is trivial.

The full abelianization of L in (1) is C3(A) x C3(B). The image of
h is zero, since h belongs to F'. The image of y is B-A, so
  [a(k)]=(k+1)A-kB.                                      (4)
For k in K, its residue modulo three is 0 or -1. Formula (4)
assigns the eta branch exactly to k=0 modulo three, and the b branch
exactly to k=-1 modulo three.

Define the closed compact spaces
  R0={(k,w) in K x F:k=0 mod 3,
                     h=w omega(w)^(-1) y^k},
  R1={(k,w) in K x F:k=-1 mod 3,
                     h=w x omega(w)^(-1) y^k}.           (5)
There is an exact homeomorphism
  R0 disjoint_union R1 -> T,       (k,w)->2k+1.            (6)
To prove both directions, the first equation in (5) is equivalent
to a(k)=w eta w^(-1), and the second to a(k)=w b w^(-1).
Either equation therefore gives D(k)=1 by (2). Conversely D(k)=1
gives the indicated factor class by (4), and then its unique
F-conjugator by (3). This proves bijectivity. The domain is compact,
the target is Hausdorff, and the displayed map is continuous, so
its inverse is continuous as well. Equivalently, the two orbit maps
F->eta^F and F->b^F are homeomorphisms onto their compact images.

The inverse in (6) reads k=(mu-1)/2, chooses its residue branch,
and reads the unique w from the corresponding actual orbit map.
Composing (6) with the frozen transporter parameterization gives
all original boundary solutions, with their exact fiber:
  (k,w,lambda) ->
     (mu,u)=(2k+1, x^k omega^2(h)^(-1) z^lambda),
                        lambda in Zhat.                 (7)
Here w is uniquely determined by k, whereas lambda records the
original right cusp-centralizer freedom. No point of either R_i
has been constructed by the free-product identification alone.

2. A useful actual section identity, before any quotient
-------------------------------------------------------
In the original E retain the proved order-three automorphism
  Omega|F=omega,  Omega(s)=y^(-1)f s.
Then Omega(xs)=fs. Put q=Omega(fs), as in the frozen class-two note.
The original normalized z-reflection has the additional exact form
  r=qz=Omega^2(s).                                       (8)
Indeed Omega(qz)=Omega^3(xs)omega(z)=(xs)x=s. Applying Omega^2
proves (8), since Omega^3=1.

There is a direct proof of the first transporter formula that now
uses only the actual coboundary equality. In E, and after the exact
quotient maps of Section 3, a coboundary solution H gives
  Omega(xs)=H^(-1)sH.
Applying Omega^2 gives
  r=omega^2(H)(xs)omega^2(H)^(-1).                        (9)
Likewise, with Y_H=H y H^(-1), direct substitution gives
  q=(omega(H)^(-1)y^(-1)H^(-1)) (Y_H s)
                         (omega(H)^(-1)y^(-1)H^(-1))^(-1).
                                                              (10)
The maps in (9)--(10) use the induced original alpha and Omega.
In E their F-conjugators are unique by D74; in a quotient these
identities remain valid without asserting uniqueness there.

3. Exact original maps to an odd-prime completion
------------------------------------------------
Fix an odd prime p. Let
  q_p:F->P=F^(p)
be the canonical maximal pro-p quotient. Its characteristic kernel
is preserved by alpha, theta and omega, so these give actual
automorphisms alpha_p, theta_p, omega_p of P. The group P is free
pro-p on x_p=q_p(x), y_p=q_p(y), by the free universal property.
The homomorphism of extensions is explicitly
  Q_p:E->E_p=P semidirect_alpha_p C2,
                   g s^epsilon -> q_p(g)s^epsilon.       (11)
The formula for Omega descends through this map. All elements f_p,
h_p,z_p and all original peripheral maps are their q_p images.

Put c_p=[x_p,y_p]. The same inverse coordinate maps as in the
class-two note give
  P/gamma3(P) <-> UT3(Z_p) <-> Z_p^3.                    (12)
For completeness, x_p^a y_p^b c_p^t fills the quotient as a compact
subgroup containing its generators; the two elementary matrices
separate the three coordinates and fill UT3(Z_p). Multiplication
is (a,b,t)(a',b',t')=(a+a',b+b',t+t'-a'b).
The map (12) is exactly the p-coordinate of F->UT3(Zhat), factored
through q_p. The original alpha_p induces (a,b,t)->(-a,-b,t).
Thus every alpha_p-fixed element has zero abelian coordinates and
lies in P'. On C_p=C_P(alpha_p) there is a continuous homomorphism
  chi_p:C_p->Z_p,
        v mod gamma3(P)=c_p^{chi_p(v)}.                  (13)

4. A split surjection from the actual pro-p fixed group
-------------------------------------------------------
Every element of a pro-p group with odd p has a unique square root.
The map is continuous: in every finite p-quotient it is the power
with exponent 2^(-1) modulo the exponent of that quotient. These
maps commute with all quotient maps and with automorphisms.

Define the explicit continuous map
  M_p:P->P,
      M_p(g)=g (g^(-1)alpha_p(g))^(1/2).                 (14)
Write a=g^(-1)alpha_p(g). Then alpha_p(a)=a^(-1), and
  alpha_p(M_p(g))=g a a^(-1/2)=M_p(g).
Also M_p(g)=g for every fixed g. Hence (14) is a continuous
retraction of spaces onto C_p. It is not being used as a group
homomorphism.

For g=c_p^u with u in Z_p, the element g^(-1)alpha_p(g) belongs to
gamma3(P), by (12). Its unique square root also lies in gamma3(P),
because it belongs to the closed procyclic subgroup generated by
that element. Therefore
  chi_p(M_p(c_p^u))=u.                                   (15)
In particular v_p=M_p(c_p) has chi_p(v_p)=1, and the continuous
homomorphism
  Z_p->C_p,           u->v_p^u                           (16)
is a right inverse to chi_p. It is injective and a homeomorphism
onto its compact image.

The original full fixed-group map is also specified:
  C_F(alpha)={1} -> C_p -> Z_p.
Its composite is zero, whereas (13) is onto by (16). Thus no

F.31: FINITE AFFINE MARGINAL IMAGES ON THE FULL PRODUCT-ONE LOCUS
Status: completed and frozen mathematical proof, exact original-word certificate, root and peer review PASS.

1. EXACT RESULT

## Actual full class-two coordinates and cyclic GT0 transporters

ACTUAL CLASS-TWO COEFFICIENT AND CYCLIC GT0 TRANSPORTERS
======================================================
Separate unnumbered proved continuation. The frozen single-parameter
note and its code/output remain unchanged. This note computes actual
quotient maps and the exact GT0 transporters. It supplies no unit in
the remaining full solution set.

1. The full class-two quotient, with inverse coordinate maps
-----------------------------------------------------------
Write gamma3(F)=closure([F',F]) and c=[x,y]=xyx^(-1)y^(-1).
The quotient Q2=F/gamma3(F) has inverse continuous coordinate maps
  Zhat^3 -> Q2, (a,b,t) -> x^a y^b c^t,
  Q2 -> Zhat^3, read (a,b,w-ab) from the matrix
                  [[1,a,w],[0,1,b],[0,0,1]].               (1)
Here the matrix map is induced by x->1+E12, y->1+E23 in
UT3(Zhat). It is onto, because these two elements and their full
profinite powers and commutator fill all such matrices.
In Q2 the commutator c is central. The set of products in the first
map is a compact subgroup containing x and y; hence it is all Q2.
Its multiplication and inverse formulas are
  (a,b,t)(a',b',t')=(a+a',b+b',t+t'-a'b),
  (a,b,t)^(-1)=(-a,-b,-t-ab).                              (2)
The matrices distinguish all three coordinates, proving injectivity
and both inverse formulas in (1). Thus F'/gamma3(F) is exactly the
full Zhat generated by c, with no prime factor omitted.

The original alpha induces
  (a,b,t) -> (-a,-b,t)                                    (3)
on Q2. Indeed f belongs to F', which is central here, so the original
generator formulas reduce to inversion of x and y. In particular
alpha fixes the c-coordinate of every element of F'. Since
f=h^(-1)alpha(h) and h belongs to F', its image under (1) is 1.
This proves the actual additional inclusion f in gamma3(F).

2. The exact class-two zero locus of the original word

  D(k)=x^k u1^(-1)z^k u2Y^(k+1),

Write the coordinates of u1 and u2 in (1) as
  u1=(a,b,t1), u2=(a,b-1,t2).                             (4)
The two abelian-coordinate equalities in (4) are precisely those
already proved from the two actual endpoint equations. The element

2. Exact filling map, all translates, and diameter equality
----------------------------------------------------------
For a nonempty compact connected A in O, Fill(A) adds the relatively
compact complementary components. An outer Euclidean annulus lies in
one complementary component; all other components have compact closure
in a smaller disk. Thus Fill(A) is compact. Each added component has
nonempty boundary in A, which proves connectedness of the filled union.

A separating ray sends every point outside conv(iota A) into the outer
component. Hence iota Fill(A) is contained in that convex hull. The
diameter of a convex hull equals the diameter of the original set by
the displayed convex-combination calculation. This gives the exact
e-diameter equality, including its reverse inclusion argument.

Every original operator q carries complement components bijectively,
and q and q^(-1) preserve compactness of their closures. The exact
maps therefore give q Fill(A)=Fill(qA). Taking the supremum of the
Euclidean diameters over every q proves
  diam_(e_Q) Fill(A)=diam_(e_Q) A.
No circle extension of q is used.

For an actual arc A with a common fixed endpoint, the compact union
A_P=A union union_u h_u(A) is connected even when P is disconnected.
Its translated union is exactly qA union union_u h_u(qA), by commutation.
The triangle inequality through the two corresponding original points
and the filling equality yield
  diam_(e_Q) Fill(A_P)
     <= diam_(e_Q) A + 2 sup_(pi A) a^+.
The estimate concerns every actual translated carrier in the original
disk. It makes no claim that these different filled sets are disjoint.

----------------------------------------
The operation begins with specified local data: an embedded closed

F_a(v)=a+(1-a)v above zero have the displayed inverse branches. The
positive bound 1-a>=1-a0 proves joint continuity of maps and inverses.

the entire disk boundary. The equivariant paste is unambiguous and
jointly continuous in O because the compact disk translates are locally

It commutes with the original Q and fixes x.

The image of K in every qD is the exact sublevel set
  v <= t a0 theta(s).
Consequently tau_t K contains K. The family

Its inverse is tau_t h_u^(-1) tau_t^(-1). Uniform continuity on the

With S=QD, the exact possible input regions are S union h_u^(-1)S

5. Actual deck-step example and its nullhomotopy
-----------------------------------------------
The example uses the original Euclidean closed disk, the exact radial

for the map and inverse sum. Pasting the triangular amplitudes on the

At a midpoint H(v_n)=qv_n. A single paste on a Q-invariant family

## Actual displacement graph and compact-family tail envelopes

UNNUMBERED GENERAL C CONTINUATION
The displacement graph and exact compact-family estimates

Author: /root/c89_review_and_general_c
Status: proved comparison in a separate note; independent mathematical audit requested.
No numbered claim is assigned here. C91, C92, the GPD precursor, and the final267 PDF remain unchanged.

PRIMARY SOURCE

work/part_c/compact_family_displacement_graph.tex
SHA256 e3f724056664f2e1e2ae164b2e046b1dd8f5cd4495a66b45866b88191ef58338
The note contains fifteen displays, CFT.1 through CFT.15.

EXACT DATA AND MAPS

The note retains all C81 data, including the original closed disk and compatible metric d, every actual operator q in Q, the transitive actual subgroup of the boundary-fixed centralizer, and the original covering pi:O->N. It uses C92's pointed identity path component I_p and exact image B_p, not a larger space of arbitrary descents. Every h_b is the unique lift lambda(b) fixing x; its inverse is lambda(b^{-1}) and it commutes with each original q.

The graph is G_p={(b,delta_b): b in B_p}, a subspace of I_p with its quotient compact-open map-and-inverse topology times C0(N) with its supremum norm. The actual forward map is Theta(a)=(D(a),delta_{D(a)}). The inverse on this exact graph is Pi(b,f)=L(b), where L is the identity extension of the unique pointed lift. Both composites are written and verified. The graph projection inverse never chooses a new deck representative.

The explicit quotient metric m uses the compact exhaustion K_n=pi psi^{-1}({|v|<=n}) and the C81 quotient metric rho. The proof checks K_n subset int K_{n+1}, cofinality for compact subsets, the metric axioms, and both directions between m convergence and the stated compact-open topology. Uniform convergence on compact sets and compact-open convergence are compared with finite compact-neighborhood tests and the positive distance between a compact image and the complement of an open neighborhood.

FINITE CORES AND INVERSE CORES

For each nonempty compact K in N, finitely many actual covering sections produce compact C in O with pi(C)=K. Then pi^{-1}(K)=QC. Equivariance and d_Q invariance give the exact equality of the supremum over pi^{-1}(K) and the maximum over C. Outside K, the triangle inequality uses the same original point z and bounds the map difference by delta_b(pi z)+delta_c(pi z). This yields CFT.5.

For a compact quotient-continuous parameter family b_u and a chosen compact core K, the inverse core is exactly K^P={b_u(y):u in P,y in K}. It is compact as a continuous image of P times K. The literal identity delta_{b_u^{-1}}=delta_{b_u} composed with b_u^{-1} proves the same inverse tail bound outside K^P. Applying the preceding finite-sheet estimate to maps and inverses gives CFT.8. No common compact support is assumed, and no quotient-distance minimizer is substituted for the fixed lift.

GRAPH TOPOLOGY AND CLOSEDNESS

The forward direction has an explicit estimate:
  ||delta_b-delta_c||_infinity <= Delta(b,c),
  m(b,c) <= d^up(b,c),
  m(b,c)+||delta_b-delta_c||_infinity <= 2 d^up(b,c).
The C92 isometry therefore proves forward continuity for the original closed-disk topology.

For the inverse, a product-convergent sequence is parameterized by P={0} union {1/n}. The displacement functions form a norm-compact subset of C0(N). A finite epsilon-net, with the union of its finitely many compact tail cores and {p}, gives a common tail. The unique lifts and inverse lifts converge uniformly on the two compact representative sets C and C^P. CFT.8 gives limsup d^up <=4 epsilon for every epsilon>0, hence convergence in the original topology. Both spaces are metrizable by the displayed metrics, so this proves inverse continuity.

Closedness is proved separately. A product limit (b,f), with b still in I_p, has delta_{b_n}(y)->delta_b(y) at each y by pointed-lift continuity. Supremum-norm convergence gives the same limit f(y). Thus f=delta_b in C0(N), b belongs to the precise image B_p, and the limit belongs to the graph. The claim is closedness in the displayed product I_p times C0(N); the proof uses no unproved identification of larger components.

COMPACT-FAMILY ENVELOPES

For a nonempty compact quotient-continuous parameter space P, define a(y)=max_u delta_{b_u}(y) and a^-(y)=max_u delta_{b_u^{-1}}(y). Joint continuity follows from the open product quotient id_P times pi applied to the actual lift displacements. A finite cover of P proves continuity of each maximum.

The note proves equivalence of four properties of this given family: continuity of L(b_u) in the original map-and-inverse topology; supremum-norm continuity of u->delta_{b_u}; a belonging to C0(N); and the common tail C92.17. It also proves the corresponding inverse tail and norm continuity through the explicit compact image core K^P.

The strictly positive auxiliary C0 function is constructed, not postulated. For the specified exhaustion, CFT.13 defines phi_n by a quotient of the rho-distance to N minus int K_{n+1} and the sum of that distance with the distance to K_n. The two closed zero sets are disjoint, so the denominator is positive. If int K_{n+1}=N, N is compact and phi_n=1 is used. Each phi_n is one on K_n and supported in K_{n+1}. The uniformly convergent series tau=sum 2^{-n}phi_n is positive everywhere and vanishes off compact sets. Thus eta=a+a^-+tau is an explicit strictly positive C0 bound for both map and inverse displacement of the original continuous compact family.

The existing C92 radial sequence, with its explicit Euclidean metric, has quotient convergence and ||delta_bR||>2/5. Its graph coordinates therefore fail to converge to (1,0), in exact agreement with its original lifts. This comparison uses the actual graph maps; it adds no new assertion about deformation existence.

The noncompact compact-support deformation remains unresolved. No scalar rescaling of the envelope is asserted to be realized by homeomorphisms. ## Exact finite pants diagram with a two-generated parity kernel

A FINITE PANTS DIAGRAM WITH A TWO-GENERATOR PARITY KERNEL
========================================================
Unnumbered exact comparison, 2026-11-13.
The group and all maps below are constructed and checked. The map from
the actual D74 extension E is not constructed. In particular the finite
parameters f*,h* below have not been identified with the images of the
actual f,h. This note tests the sufficiency of listed finite constraints;
it does not assert a counterexample to D74.40 or replace the actual tau.

1. Completely enumerated base data
----------------------------------
Let G=GL(3,F2), acting on the seven nonzero binary vectors numbered 1--7.
The checker constructs G from all 512 binary matrices and their actual
permutations. It proves by finite enumeration:
  |G|=168; G is nonabelian simple and perfect;
  its involutions form one class I of size 21;
  all 179 subgroups are enumerated;
  every proper subgroup is soluble, of derived length at most three;
  every proper subgroup contains at most nine involutions.
There are 19,152 ordered generating pairs, with 57 automorphism orbits,
and 2,352 generating involution triples, with seven automorphism orbits.
There are 3,696 generating pairs (x,y) for which x,y,xy each belong to
I I, and these form eleven automorphism orbits.

The complete automorphism group, of order 336, is computed without a
classification theorem. Fix one generating pair and a spanning tree in
its two-generator labelled Cayley graph. For every ordered generating
target pair, the tree uniquely prescribes a possible map G->G. The
checker verifies every edge labelled by either generator. Passing that
test proves the map respects right multiplication by every word, hence
every group element. Its image contains the target generators, so it
is onto and therefore an automorphism. Conversely every automorphism
occurs from its images of the fixed generating pair. Thus the finite
list is complete. All tuple orbits have size 336, as independently
verified in the enumeration.

Select the first eight representatives of the eleven three-cusp pair
orbits in the output. They are pairwise inequivalent under every
automorphism of G. Write them (x_j,y_j), 0<=j<8, and put
z_j=(x_j y_j)^(-1). Their rotation orders are, respectively,
  (4,4,4), (4,3,3), (4,4,4), (4,3,3),
  (4,4,3), (4,3,4), (3,4,4), (3,4,3).
All exact permutations and indices are retained in the output.

2. Exact parity-kernel and four-factor maps
-----------------------------------------
Let V=C2^3 with basis e0,e1,e2 and set
  A*=G^8 x V,
  epsilon:A*->C2, epsilon(g,v)=v0+v1+v2,
  K*=ker(epsilon)=G^8 x W0,
  X=((x_j)_j,e1+e0), Y=((y_j)_j,e2+e0).
Then X,Y generate K*. Here is the exact subgroup argument. A proper
subdirect subgroup of G^r has a relation g_j=sigma(g_i) for two
coordinates and an automorphism sigma of G: induct on r, and when the

At the cocycle level, zero summed restriction therefore makes every
cocycle principal, d_j=b_j*(chi_j-1). Nontrivial C makes their sum
vanish on K exactly when sum_j b_j=0. The kernel has dimension
m-1 on 7m coordinates, so the exact rank is 6m+1.

A cocycle with trace-zero restriction gives the tuple (d^(q1^j))_j
and hence is principal. Its parameter has trace zero because C is
nontrivial. Conversely those principal cocycles have zero trace.
This establishes precisely the trace-kernel equality of F.26 for
the present locus. The F.26 reduction sends every proper original
affine marginal image to a nonprincipal trace-kernel element over
the same scalar field and retains the original scalar character.
The proved equality excludes it, even when the original coefficient
field is larger. The exact F.23 sign isomorphism transports the
negative image equality to the stated positive coordinates.

1. EXACT RESULT

and R_- on the locus

Put q1=|k1|, m=[k0:k1], r_j=r^(q1^j), t_j=t^(q1^j), and
chi_j=chi^(q1^j). The actual coefficient map d->d^(q1^j), with

Every invariant subspace with no proper nonzero invariant subspace
either lies in W_j or meets W_j trivially. In the latter case pi_j

For a nonzero intertwiner between two such subspaces, scalar source

  W versus W: sources 0 and 7 determine r_j and t_j, hence j=l.

Since c!=1, all the indicated contradictions are valid. Inverse

6. SUMMED RESTRICTION AND THE FINITE AFFINE CONSEQUENCE

The summed restriction direct_sum_j Q_j -> H1_cont(K,k0_chi|K)
is well typed because all characters agree on K. It commutes with
the actual source precomposition operators. Each individual restriction
is injective by F.24 because its scalar character on R is the same

A nonzero invariant kernel would contain a nonzero invariant subspace
T of smallest dimension. Every nonzero coordinate projection p_j|T
is injective. Two such projections would produce the actual

is p_j composed with (p_l|T)^-1. All cross-factor comparisons exclude
this. Thus T has only one nonzero coordinate, where individual F.24
restriction injectivity excludes it. The summed H1 restriction is
therefore injective.

Zero summed cocycle restriction consequently forces d_j=b_j*(chi_j-1).
Since the common character on K is nontrivial, their parameter sum
must be zero. Conversely those tuples have zero summed restriction.
The kernel has dimension m-1 on 7m columns, proving rank 6m+1.

A trace-zero cocycle gives the Frobenius tuple (d^(q1^j))_j and
hence is principal, with trace-zero parameter. This proves exactly
the trace kernel of F.26 on the present locus. Every proper original
affine marginal image would give a nonprincipal such cocycle through
the F.26 conjugation and coefficient homomorphism. Those explicit maps
retain the original scalar character and thus preserve the locus and
fields. The trace result excludes every proper image, even for a larger
original coefficient field. The F.23 based isomorphism and inverse
carry the actual negative K/R pair to the positive pair and complete

A. Full centralizers and normalizers of the actual image cusps
-------------------------------------------------------------
Here is the elementary centralizer argument used for these images.
Use a full free profinite group W and an element t in W admitting a
continuous character chi:W->Zhat with chi(t)=1. The instances below
are R, F0, and the explicitly identified F_* in Section E. The power map
Zhat-><t>, lambda->t^lambda, is an isomorphism: composition with chi
is the identity. Set C=C_W(t), K_t=ker(chi|C). The explicit inverse
continuous maps
  K_t x <t> -> C, (k,t^lambda) -> k t^lambda,
  C -> K_t x <t>, u -> (u t^(-chi(u)),t^chi(u))
give C=K_t x <t>.

For completeness K_t is trivial. A nontrivial profinite K_t has a
nontrivial finite quotient, so for some prime p one of its pro-p Sylow
subgroups is nontrivial. Choose a nonidentity element v in that
subgroup. The free profinite W has cd_p(W)=1; consequently it has no
element of order p. The closed subgroup <v> is therefore Z_p. The
p-factor <t>_p is another Z_p, centralizes <v>, and has trivial
intersection with it by chi. Thus multiplication embeds the compact
group Z_p x Z_p as a closed subgroup of W. Its nonzero degree-two
cohomology contradicts cd_p(W)=1 and inheritance of that bound by
closed subgroups. Hence
  C_W(t)=<t>.
For u in N_W(<t>), write u t u^(-1)=t^lambda with
lambda in Zhat^times. Applying chi gives lambda=1, so also
  N_W(<t>)=<t>.                                             (A1)
This argument concerns the entire generator t. No assertion about
centralizers of individual p-components or malnormality is made.

For i(c_j), use the character on R obtained from q4|R followed by,
respectively, the x-coordinate, the y-coordinate, or minus the
x-coordinate of F_ab. It takes value 1 on the indicated element.
For tau(c_j), use the corresponding character on F0; the identity
abelianization of tau gives the same value 1. Thus (A1) applies to
all six actual image elements.

Choose an actual reflection r_j in D_j. The maps i and tau preserve
parity, so i(r_j) and tau(r_j) are outside the respective parity
kernels, have order two, and invert their image rotations. Every
normalizer element inside the parity kernel is a rotation by (A1).
Multiplication by the displayed reflection sends every outside
normalizer element inside. Therefore the exact full normalizers are
  N_P4(i(L_j))=i(L_j) semidirect <i(r_j)>=i(D_j),
  N_P3(tau(L_j))=tau(L_j) semidirect <tau(r_j)>=tau(D_j).     (A2)
The restriction tau|D_j is injective: a kernel element cannot have
odd parity; a rotation c_j^lambda in its kernel has lambda=0 after
applying the character. Compactness then makes it a homeomorphism
onto the closed subgroup in (A2). In particular rho|i(D_j) is the
specified isomorphism onto tau(D_j), for all three original cusps.

Equation (A2) identifies normalizers of the image cusps. It has not
identified those cusps with the standard <X0>,<U0>,<Z0> in P3.
Moreover the already proved abelianization of tau fixes any possible
unit exponent in such an identification: writing tau(x) as a

The analogous calculation applies separately to y and z. No such
conjugacy is established here.

## Literal full and pro-two coproduct comparison

Explicit comparison of the two coproducts
----------------------------------------
Take the actual groups
  P_all=C2(a)*C2(b) in the full profinite category,
  P_2=C2(a2)*_pro2 C2(b2) in the pro-2 category.
There are explicit mutually inverse maps identifying
  P_all = Zhat(t) semidirect_-1 C2(a), t=ba,
  P_2   = Z2(t2) semidirect_-1 C2(a2), t2=b2 a2.
For the first equality, send a to (0,1), b to (1,1), and in the
reverse direction send (lambda,epsilon) to (ba)^lambda a^epsilon.
The latter map is a homomorphism because a(ba)a=(ba)^(-1).
Both composites fix the displayed generators. The same two formulas
over Z2 give the second equality by the pro-2 coproduct universal
property. All maps are continuous.

The factor-preserving comparison map is the surjection
  kappa:P_all -> P_2,
  kappa(a)=a2, kappa(b)=b2,
  kappa(lambda,epsilon)=(lambda_2,epsilon).
Its exact kernel, with the displayed embeddings, is
  ker(kappa)=(product over odd primes l of Z_l) x {0}.        (W1)
For example the 3-primary idempotent e_3 in Zhat gives a nonidentity
kernel element t^e_3.

An executed finite witness is the full continuous quotient
  P_all -> S3, a->(12), b->(23).
The product t=ba maps to (132), of order three; the two factor images
generate all six elements of S3. Hence t^e_3 has that same nonidentity
image. This quotient does not factor through kappa, since a continuous
finite image of P_2 is a 2-group. This proves the nontrivial comparison
kernel by an explicit actual homomorphism as well as by (W1).

The relative projective-pair property holds for this actual P_2
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Here is a direct finite lifting argument in Wilkes Definitions 6.1--6.2,
with no use of his Theorem 6.9. Let pi:B->A be a finite surjection,
phi:P_2->A a continuous homomorphism, and sigma_i:C2(i)->B the two
specified local lifts. Replace A by phi(P_2), a 2-group, and B by its
inverse image. Put K=ker(pi). A 2-Sylow subgroup S of B maps onto A,
so B=SK. Each sigma_i(C2(i)) is a 2-subgroup of B. Sylow conjugacy
puts it into S by some element of B; writing that element as s k
with s in S and k in K shows that a K-conjugation already puts it
into S. Thus choose k_i in K with
  sigma'_i=k_i sigma_i k_i^(-1):C2(i)->S.
The actual pro-2 coproduct universal property gives gamma:P_2->S
extending these two homomorphisms. Composing with S->B supplies
  pi gamma=phi,
  gamma|C2(i)=k_i sigma_i k_i^(-1).
The first equality holds on both factors, which topologically generate
P_2. These are the exact relative lifting equalities; the inverse k_i
are Wilkes's displayed local comparison conjugators. Thus this pair
satisfies the projective profinite-pair property of his part (II).

Interpreting part (III) literally as a full coproduct, even with an
additional free pro-2 factor, would give a full continuous quotient
onto S3: use (12),(23) on the two C2 factors and kill that extra
factor. The actual P_2 has no such quotient. The comparison (W1)
and the preceding lifting proof therefore exhibit the precise failure
of that literal full-coproduct reading. No replacement source wording
or conjecture about the author's intention is used.

or P4 in the pants construction with any pro-2 completion. The frozen

1. An actual permutation inequality, with all subgroup maps
----------------------------------------------------------
Keep E, F, T_i=<t_i> (i=0,1,2), and k=F2 from D74/D76. Let q:E->A
be any continuous onto map to a finite group. Let Omega=A/M be a
transitive A-set, n=|Omega|, and let U=q^(-1)(M). The explicit map
  E/U -> A/M, gU -> q(g)M
is an equivariant bijection. Thus [E:U]=n. Define
  f_i=|Fix_Omega(q(t_i))|, S=f_0+f_1+f_2.

Restrict the actual D76 exact sequence to U:
  0 -> Delta_T -> P=direct_sum_i k[[E/T_i]] -> k -> 0,
  Delta_T|U = k[[U]]^(2n).
The second equality uses D76's full Delta_T ~= k[[E]]^2 and the
finite coset decomposition of the free k[[U]]-module k[[E]].
For every double coset U g T_i, the map
  U/(U cap g T_i g^(-1)) -> U g T_i/T_i,
  u(U cap g T_i g^(-1)) -> u g T_i
is an equivariant homeomorphism. Inversion U g -> g^(-1)U identifies
the right T_i-orbits on U\E with its left orbits on E/U. Hence f_i
of these U-orbits have stabilizer a full C2 and (n-f_i)/2 have trivial
stabilizer. This includes the case q(t_i)=1.

  dim H_1(U,P)=S,
  dim H_0(U,P)=(3n+S)/2,
  dim H_0(U,Delta_T)=2n,

All terms and arrows are restrictions or derived coinvariants of the
original sequence, with no replacement of the stabilizer U. Exactness
proves

finite computation is offered as evidence for this topological theorem.

## Exact trace obstruction and all scalar-field-nine affine images

F.26: EXACT TRACE OBSTRUCTION AND SCALAR-FIELD-NINE AFFINE IMAGES
Status: completed proof; final source frozen after root mathematical review.

1. RESULT AND SCOPE

For the actual inclusions mathcal K_sign <= R_sign <= V_sign retained
from F.19--F.25, every continuous affine representation over a finite
field whose scalar values generate a subfield of order nine has equal
images of mathcal K_sign and R_sign. This includes every representation
V_sign -> Aff_1(F9): scalar field F3 is covered by F.25, and scalar field
F9 is proved here. The original coefficient field may be larger than F9.
Both signs are covered through the actual based isomorphism of F.23.13.

The proof also establishes an exact trace reduction for every proper
finite scalar-affine marginal image. It gives an equivalence with a
trace-cocycle kernel problem, with all coefficient maps and their
inverses specified. The arbitrary-field kernel problem, full marginal
equality mathcal K_sign = R_sign, and the original K+ = D+ remain open.
No claim about those unresolved equalities follows from the finite F9
enumeration alone. This statement contains no new literature input.

2. ACTUAL IMAGE REDUCTION

Write H = rho(V), N = rho(R), M = rho(K), D = chi(V), C = chi(R).
The actual F.21 normal generation, followed by the actual F.22
surjection D+ -> R, gives normal_N(M) = N and chi(K) = chi(R) = C.
Thus C = 1 implies image equality directly in the abelian group N.

For a proper marginal, C is nontrivial and cyclic. Choose an actual
lift (b,c) in M of a generator c of C. Conjugation by the inverse of
the translation tau_z, z = b/(1-c), makes M_z = U semidirect C.
The subgroup U consists of the original translations and is linear
over k1 = F_p(C). Put k0 = F_p(D). Normality of N in H makes the
translation groups A_H and A_N vector spaces over k0. The exact
commutator [(a,1),(0,c)] = ((1-c)a,1) proves A_H = A_N = A.
For an arbitrary (b',d) in H_z the commutator with (0,c) likewise
equals ((1-c)b',1); hence b' lies in A. This proves the literal
decompositions H_z = A semidirect D, N_z = A semidirect C,
M_z = U semidirect C, with U properly contained in A.

Choose a k1-linear functional L on the coefficient field, zero on U
and nonzero on A, by extending a basis. The trace polynomial
Tr(x) = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} x^(q1^j), with m = [k0:k1], is nonzero
because its degree is smaller than |k0|. Its values lie in k1, so it
is onto. If Tr(beta)=1, then Tr(a*(beta/a))=1 for every a != 0.
This proves the nondegenerate trace pairing in every characteristic,
including characteristics dividing m.

Choose a k0-basis v_i of the original coefficient field. The trace
pairing supplies unique a_i with L(t*v_i) = Tr(a_i*t). Set
ell(sum_i t_i*v_i) = sum_i a_i*t_i. Then ell is k0-linear,
L = Tr composed with ell, ell(A)=k0, and ell(U) lies in ker Tr.
The map (b,d) -> (ell(b),d) is an actual affine-group homomorphism.
Composing with the specified conjugation and rho gives rho' with

  rho'(V) = k0 semidirect D,
  rho'(R) = k0 semidirect C,
  rho'(K) <= ker(Tr:k0->k1) semidirect C.

All scalar values and the original character are retained. All finite
group and field maps are continuous, and their composites with the
original profinite representations are continuous. F.25 already
excludes k0=k1 for a proper image, so the reduction has k1 < k0.

3. EXACT TRACE CRITERION AND COEFFICIENT SPLITTING

Because chi(K) lies in k1, the map

  T_chi: Z1_cont(V,k0_chi) -> Z1_cont(K,k1_chi|K),
  d -> Tr(d|K)

is a well-typed linear map of continuous cocycle spaces. Its principal
kernel subspace is P_chi = { b*(chi-1) : Tr(b)=0 }, of k1-dimension
m-1. The preceding proper-image reduction supplies a nonprincipal
element of ker T_chi. Conversely every element of ker T_chi outside
P_chi gives the actual affine representation g -> (d(g),chi(g)).
Its translation group is a k0-subspace of k0. If it were zero, a
generator lift of the cyclic scalar image would have a fixed point,
making d principal; trace vanishing on K and nontrivial C would then
put its parameter in ker Tr, a contradiction. Thus all translations
occur, the R image is k0 semidirect C by the same commutator, and
the K image lies in the proper trace-kernel subgroup. This proves
both directions of the exact criterion.

The field isomorphism

  k0 tensor_{k1} k0 -> product_{j=0}^{m-1} k0,
  b tensor a -> (a*b^(q1^j))_j

has an explicit Lagrange-interpolation inverse, using the distinct
Frobenius conjugates of a multiplicative generator of k0. With the
chi action on the first tensor factor, these are the distinct
characters chi_j = chi^(q1^j), which agree on R. The proof applies
this map to all seven cocycle coordinates of V = free profinite F7.
For the actual subgroup K, coefficient projections in a finite
field basis preserve continuity and cocycles. The scalar extension
of T_chi becomes (d_j)_j -> sum_j d_j|K, and that of P_chi is
{ (b_j*(chi_j-1))_j : sum_j b_j=0 }. Field extension preserves
kernels and detects nonzero vector spaces. The remaining exact
rank target is therefore 6m+1 on 7m columns. General attainment
of this rank has not been proved.

4. EXHAUSTIVE F9 SCOPE AND COEFFICIENT COMPARISON

The programs use F9 = F3[i]/(i^2+1), encoding a+b*i by a+3*b.
The polynomial has no F3 root, so this is a field. For any other
field k0 of order nine, choose an element i0 of order four and use
the actual isomorphism a+b*i -> a+b*i0; the inverse records the
two basis coefficients. Applying this map to both affine coordinates
identifies the representations and the two subgroup images exactly.

Here Tr(a+b*i)=2*a and Tr(i*(a+b*i))=b. Thus multiplication by i
is the coefficient isomorphism from the computed imaginary-part
kernel to the trace kernel, and multiplication by -i is its inverse.
Real principal parameters go to the trace-zero line F3*i. The
independent verifier checks the identity on all nine field elements.

F.25 covers C=1 and k0=k1. The remaining scalar-field-nine case
has k1=F3, C={1,-1}. The four deleted generator values are in
{1,-1} and not all one: 15 choices. Normal generation of R by
the deleted generators identifies their scalar subgroup with C.
The three retained values range over (F9*)^3 minus (F3*)^3:
504 choices. Those values generate F9, since its degree over F3
is two. Hence exactly 15*504=7560 tuples exhaust the remaining
class; this is a full enumeration, not a sample.

5. EXACT FINITE CALCULATIONS

The first producer evaluates all 64 literal F.24 source rows at
each tuple. For a row a=a_r+i*a_i and cocycle vector v=x+i*y,
Im(a*v)=0 is the F3-linear equation (a_i,a_r)*(x,y)^T=0.
All these rows kill the nonzero principal vector t-1. Exact rank
counts on fourteen columns are 11:8, 12:396, 13:7156. Thus 7156
tuples already have precisely the one-dimensional principal kernel.
The remaining 404 tuples are listed explicitly in the first output.

The second producer evaluates all eleven actual old-source matrices
from F.24 and the eight negative seed rows. It expands A=B+i*C as
the F3 block matrix [[B,-C],[C,B]] and repeatedly computes
W -> W + sum_i W*A_i. Every resulting row lies in the F3-linear
span of imaginary-part evaluation rows of actual source conjugates
of the seeds. The source action preserves the character and the
actual subgroup K. Exact ranks across the 404 tuples are:

  Eight seed rows: 5:80, 6:284, 7:2, 8:38.
  One closure round: 12:50, 13:354.
  Two closure rounds: 13:404.
  Third round: 13:404, stable under all eleven matrices.

The matrices are invertible because they come from actual source
automorphisms. Stable finite-dimensional spaces are also invariant
under their inverses. In particular every required actual vanishing
condition implies membership in the proved one-dimensional kernel.
Conversely that principal line vanishes on K because chi(K) is real.
The explicit multiplication-by-i comparison gives ker T_chi=P_chi.
The trace criterion then proves the scalar-field-nine equality.

6. INDEPENDENT AUDIT AND FILE BINDINGS

The root independent verifier imports neither producer. It uses
multiplicative-log Laurent evaluation and scalar incremental F3
echelon elimination, independently of the producers' field-table
evaluation and batched row reduction. It verifies all 7560 tuples,
their nonzero principal vectors, all eleven source actions for the
404 remaining tuples, every closure image, all rank distributions,
stable row spaces, and all nine Im/Tr coefficient identities.
Its status is PASS_INDEPENDENT_EXHAUSTIVE_F9. Its output SHA256 is
cd9a2398fe437a08b47dd892b27a556fce102b602318683b1f8be25a9991433f.
The universal Laurent source rows/actions used by both calculations
are the literal source data already independently audited in F.24.

The manifest binds the proof, metadata, this report, F.21--F.25
dependencies, the actual F.23 braid input, universal F.24 source
data, both F9 producers with their outputs/stdout, the complete
trace-reduction research proof, and all five files in the root
independent-audit directory. The research-stage statuses inside the
older producer outputs are preserved faithfully; the completed
written proof and independent audit supply the present claim.

Root reviewed the complete mathematical proof and requested only
the row-span precision repair after F.26.23, applied in the frozen

The general unequal-field rank problem is retained explicitly as

## Actual section lifts, labelled retraction and finite peripheral obstructions

PANTS SECTION LIFTS AND THE ACTUAL PERIPHERAL COMPARISON
======================================================
Unnumbered research note. No frozen source or registered claim is changed.
The existence question in D74.40 remains unresolved in this note.

Source data fixed throughout
---------------------------
Use the actual D74 group
  F = Fhat(x,y), z=(xy)^(-1), E=F semidirect_alpha <s>,
  alpha(x)=x^(-1), alpha(y)=f^(-1)y^(-1)f, f in F', alpha^2=1.
D74 proves that all three full involution classes have centralizer C2,
that E is real projective, and that the exact equation
  f=h^(-1)alpha(h)
has its unique solution h in F'. In particular alpha(f)=f^(-1).
Put Y=h y h^(-1). The actual involutions
  t0=s, t1=xs, t2=Ys
represent the three classes. Write Ti=<ti>.
Their images in A0=H_1(E,F2), with coordinates (x,y,s), are respectively
  (0,0,1), (1,0,1), (0,1,1).
They are pairwise distinct. A0 is the actual elementary abelian quotient
of E, not a substituted free-product model.

The original peripheral subgroups and normalizers are
  Lx=<x>, Ly=<y>, Lz=<z>, Dj=N_E(Lj).
Thus Dx=<s,xs> and Dy=<fs,yfs> are the actual full dihedral groups,
with rotations x and y. The two classes in Dz are the t1 and t2 classes.
The relation xyz=1 remains an equality of these original elements.

A. A stronger, proved lifting property of the three actual sections
-----------------------------------------------------------------
For every finite surjection pi:B->A, continuous phi:E->A, and specified
homomorphisms sigma_i:Ti->B satisfying pi sigma_i=phi|Ti, there are
  gamma:E->B and k_i in ker(pi)
such that
  pi gamma=phi,
  gamma(t_i)=k_i sigma_i(t_i) k_i^(-1), i=0,1,2.                (A1)
Neither gamma nor the sigma_i are required to be onto. A sigma_i may
be trivial. This is an unconditional property of the actual D74 E.

Here are all finite refinements and maps proving it. Replace A by phi(E)
and B by its inverse image; this preserves ker(pi) and the local maps.
For each i the clopen compact set
  Wi=E \ (Ti ker(phi))
contains no element centralizing t_i, because C_E(t_i)=Ti. For each g
in Wi, choose an open normal subgroup N_i,g of E contained in
ker(phi) cap F cap ker(E->A0), with [g,t_i] not in N_i,g. The coset
g N_i,g still has this property. Finitely many such cosets cover Wi.
Intersect these finitely many open normal subgroups for all three i;
when a Wi is empty it contributes no conditions. The resulting N gives
  q:E->J=E/N, lambda:J->A, lambda q=phi,
and satisfies
  lambda(C_J(q(t_i))) <= phi(Ti).                             (A2)
Indeed a lift g of a finite centralizer element cannot belong to Wi.
Also q(t_i) are nonidentity and pairwise nonconjugate: their images in
the actual quotient A0 remain the three distinct displayed vectors.

Form the finite pullback
  Bhat = {(b,j) in B x J : pi(b)=lambda(j)},
  p:Bhat->J, p(b,j)=j,
  beta:Bhat->B, beta(b,j)=b.
Both coordinate maps are continuous homomorphisms; p is onto. Set
  b_i=(sigma_i(t_i),q(t_i)) in Bhat,
  C=union_i {v b_i v^(-1):v in Bhat}.
Each b_i has order exactly two, even when sigma_i is trivial. Every
involution t in E is g t_i g^(-1) for some i,g. Lift q(g) through p;
conjugating b_i by that lift shows q(t) lies in p(C). Moreover no
q(t) is trivial. These are exactly the data of Haran 1990 Definition
1.1(4), and D74 real projectivity plus Proposition 2.3 supplies
  Gamma:E->Bhat, p Gamma=q, Gamma(Inv(E)) subset C.             (A3)

Since the three q(t_i) are nonconjugate, for each i there is v_i in
Bhat with Gamma(t_i)=v_i b_i v_i^(-1); the factor index must be i.
Then p(v_i) centralizes q(t_i). By (A2), choose epsilon_i in {0,1}
with lambda(p(v_i))=phi(t_i)^epsilon_i. Define
  gamma=beta Gamma,
  k_i=beta(v_i) sigma_i(t_i)^(-epsilon_i).
We have pi(k_i)=1. Multiplication by this power does not change the
conjugation of sigma_i(t_i), so (A1) follows. This also handles
phi(t_i)=1 and sigma_i(t_i)=1 without changing any domain.

The same property holds for a surjection of arbitrary profinite groups
pi:B->A with the same specified maps. For each open normal V of B use
the finite problem
  B/V -> A/pi(V), phi_V, (sigma_i)_V.
Its kernel is (ker(pi)V)/V. The sets of solutions, including the three
kernel conjugators, are finite and nonempty: E is generated by x,y,s.
Reduction carries solutions at finer V to solutions at coarser V.
A common refinement solves every finite collection of compatibility
requirements. Compactness gives compatible solutions at all V, whose
inverse limits are the required continuous gamma and k_i in ker(pi).
The sets pi(V) form a neighbourhood basis in A, so pi gamma=phi
as actual profinite maps. This supplies the inverse-limit step directly.

Consequently (E,{T0,T1,T2}) has Wilkes's projective-pair lifting property
(Definitions 6.1--6.2 of the retained 2209.06492v1). The proof just given
uses the actual centralizers and Haran's restricted involution lifts;
it does not infer full pair projectivity from cohomological vanishing.

B. The precise cohomological comparison
---------------------------------------
D76.15 proves H^2(E,{Ti};M)=0 for every finite F2[E]-module M. For an
odd prime p and finite Fp[E]-module M, the actual index-two extension
has
  H^n(E,M)=H^n(F,M)^{C2}=0 for n>=2,
since averaging by 1/2 kills the positive C2 rows and cd_p(F)=1.
Also H^n(Ti,M)=0 for n>=1. The actual relative long exact sequence
therefore gives H^2(E,{Ti};M)=0 at every odd p. A filtration of a
finite abelian E-module by its primary and elementary-abelian layers,
and exactness in the coefficient module, gives the same vanishing for
every finite abelian E-module.

Wilkes Proposition 6.3 identifies this vanishing with the solvability
of the specified relative problems having finite abelian kernel.
Corollary 6.4 records that equivalence. His Proposition 6.6 promotes
the property through solvable kernels in its prosolvable setting.
Proposition 6.8 constructs its free-product map for a pro-p group and
uses its H_1 isomorphism to prove surjectivity; Theorem 6.9 retains that
pro-p hypothesis. Section A above gives a stronger finite lifting fact
for this E, but supplies no such surjectivity argument for the actual
full free-product comparison below.

C. An actual labelled retract of four involutions and a map to three
------------------------------------------------------------------
Let P4 be the full free profinite product of the four specified groups
C2(a), C2(b), C2(c), C2(d). The continuous homomorphism
  q4:P4->E,
  (a,b,c,d) |-> (s,xs,fs,yfs)                                 (C1)
is onto: ba maps to x, dc maps to y, and a maps to s. All four target
elements are involutions; this follows directly from the alpha formulas
and alpha(f)=f^(-1).

Its parity kernel P4+ is the full free profinite group on
  X=ba, U=dc, V=ca.
For an explicit proof, let R=Fhat(X,U,V) and define the involution
  delta(X)=X^(-1), delta(V)=V^(-1),
  delta(U)=V^(-1)U^(-1)V.
The maps
  P4 -> R semidirect_delta <a>,
      (a,b,c,d) |-> (a,Xa,Va,UVa),
  R semidirect_delta <a> -> P4,
      (X,U,V,a) |-> (ba,dc,ca,a)
are inverse continuous homomorphisms. Each named generator maps back
to itself, delta^2=1, and the three products Xa,Va,UVa have square one.
Thus these maps prove the kernel and basis assertion without changing
from the full profinite category.

On this exact kernel, q4 has the maps
  q4|P4+:Fhat(X,U,V)->Fhat(x,y),
  X|->x, U|->y, V|->f.
Its kernel is exactly the closed normal closure in P4+ of
  V f(X,U)^(-1).                                              (C2)
Indeed quotienting by this element eliminates V and gives the inverse
map Fhat(x,y)->P4+/ker(q4), x|->X, y|->U. The kernel is invariant
under delta because q4 intertwines delta with alpha.

Put H=h(X,U), so q4(H)=h. For the three Ti in section A choose the
specified lifts
  t0|->a, t1|->b, t2|->H d H^(-1).
For the last equality, in E one has
  h(yfs)h^(-1)=h y f alpha(h)^(-1)s=h y h^(-1)s=Ys.
Apply section A's profinite lifting property to pi=q4 and phi=id_E.
It gives a continuous section
  i:E->P4, q4 i=id_E,
and k_i in ker(q4) which conjugate these three specified local lifts
to i(t_i). In particular i is injective. Conjugating i by an element
of ker(q4) arranges i(s)=a, while retaining q4 i=id_E and the other
two labelled conjugacy conclusions.

Now define the actual full free product P3=C2(a)*C2(b)*C2(d) and fold
  rho:P4->P3, (a,b,c,d)|->(a,b,a,d).
It preserves parity. Its restriction to the parity kernels is
  Fhat(X,U,V)->Fhat(X0=ba,U0=da),
  (X,U,V)|->(X0,U0,1).
The continuous map
  tau=rho i:E->P3                                             (C3)
sends the actual F into P3+=Fhat(X0,U0), maps s to a, and satisfies
  tau|F composed with alpha = delta0 composed with tau|F,
where delta0 inverts X0 and U0. It sends the three full involution
classes to their respective a,b,d classes, by the displayed lifts.

On full abelianizations identify F_ab with Zhat^2 via x,y and P3+_ab
with Zhat^2 via X0,U0. The maps (q4|P4+)_ab and (rho|P4+)_ab have
the same matrix (X,U,V)|->(x,y,0), because f lies in F'. Hence
  (tau|F)_ab = identity on Zhat^2.                             (C4)
This also proves that the induced map on each maximal pro-p quotient
is an automorphism, by the Frattini criterion and finite-generation
Hopficity for the two free pro-p groups. Formula (C4) is a statement
about the actual homomorphism (C3), before taking any pro-p quotient.

The unproved points in this comparison are precise. We have not proved
that tau|F is injective or onto, or that tau maps the original x,y,z
to conjugates of a common unit power of X0,U0,(X0 U0)^(-1).
For example, after i(s)=a the first image has the actual form
  tau(x)=rho(k_1) b rho(k_1)^(-1) a,
for a kernel conjugator k_1. Section A supplies no equality of this
element with a conjugate of X0^mu. The maps (C1)--(C4) therefore do
not establish a solution of D74.40. D77 only addresses its specified
arbitrary representatives; its failed y-cusp alignment is retained.

D. Executed finite tests of the full peripheral lifting step
------------------------------------------------------------
D.1. A finite abelian kernel, with incompatible shared endpoints.
The distinction needed here is expressed by one actual commuting
diagram and a proved obstruction, not by omitting the peripheral maps.
Set
  A=A0=F2^3, coordinates (x,y,s),
  B=F2^4, basis (a,b,c,d), written additively,
  pi(a)=pi(c)=sbar,
  pi(b)=xbar+sbar, pi(d)=ybar+sbar.
This is an onto finite homomorphism with
  ker(pi)=<a+c> of order two.
Let phi:E->A be its actual mod-two abelianization.

Choose b_z in Dz in the t1 class; D34's original triangle supplies
this endpoint. Thus phi(b_z)=xbar+sbar. On the three full dihedral
groups specify the continuous homomorphisms

  source       rotation image in B      reflection image in B
  Dx           x |-> a+b                s |-> a
  Dy           y |-> c+d               fs |-> c
  Dz           z |-> b+d              b_z |-> b.

Each map factors through the actual quotient of Zhat semidirect C2
which reduces the rotation exponent modulo two; its target is an
elementary abelian group. The involution, inversion and square
relations therefore hold, and pi sigma_j=phi|Dj on both generators.
Their local endpoint classes use precisely the original triangle.

There is no continuous gamma:E->B with pi gamma=phi which agrees
with all these sigma_j, even allowing ker(pi)-conjugation. The latter
conjugations are trivial since B is abelian. The actual relation
xyz=1 would give
  0=gamma(x)+gamma(y)+gamma(z)
   =(a+b)+(c+d)+(b+d)=a+c,
contradicting the nonzero kernel generator. Already the first two
local maps conflict: fs=h^(-1)sh in E, whereas their prescribed
abelian images are respectively c and a.

For comparison, the three individual sections t0,t1,t2 with images
a,b,d do have a global lift. It is the homomorphism through A with
  gamma(s)=a, gamma(x)=a+b, gamma(y)=a+d.                     (D1)
Since h is a commutator, gamma(t2)=gamma(Ys)=d. Thus the three
section assignments commute with pi and are simultaneously realized,
while the stated additional original-y dihedral map is not.

This is a deliberately specified incompatible relative lift problem.
It is not a counterexample to D74.40, and gives no counterexample to
the existence of compatible peripheral choices. It proves exactly
that section A's universal relative lifting statement cannot be
promoted to arbitrary specified lifts of all three original Dj.

Executed verification:

The code checks all 256 addition pairs for pi, each local quotient

D.2. An A5 kernel, compatible endpoint classes, and injective local

The following stronger obstruction retains compatibility of all endpoint

Let A=(Z/6)^2 semidirect_{-1} C2, with the fully specified operation

The actual homomorphism
  phi:E->A,

exists because alpha induces inversion on the full F_ab and f is a

Thus |A|=72, |B|=4320 and |K|=60.

Permutations below act on {1,2,3,4,5}; multiplication is composition,
with the right factor applied first. Define
  a=(12)(34), b=(13)(24), c=(12)(35),
  R=ba=(14)(23), Z=ca=(345).

  rho_x(x)=R, rho_x(s)=a;

In each case a has order two and conjugates the stated rotation to
its inverse. The rotation orders are respectively 2,2,3. These are
therefore homomorphisms of the full Dj, not just assignments to a
pro-p or discrete quotient. Define the precise local lift maps
  sigma_j:Dj->B, d|->(rho_j(d),phi(d)).                        (D4)
Then pi sigma_j=phi|Dj.

Each rotation phi(x),phi(y),phi(z) has order six, and the chosen
reflection has nontrivial C2-coordinate. Therefore
  ker(phi|Dj)=<c_j^6>, where (c_x,c_y,c_z)=(x,y,z).
Every rho_j kills this subgroup because its rotation order divides
six. It follows that pi maps sigma_j(Dj) isomorphically onto phi(Dj),
both of order twelve. Equivalently sigma_j(Dj) is the graph of a
specified homomorphism phi(Dj)->A5. This verifies the local-injectivity
condition also used in the Haran--Jarden embedding-problem convention.

All six canonical endpoint images under the first components are
nontrivial involutions of A5. In the e_2 representatives they are
  Dx: (a,b), Dy: (a,b), Dz: (a,a).
For the last pair e_2 is zero modulo three, so rho_z(z^{e_2})=1;
this finite fusion is retained explicitly. All fifteen involutions
of A5 are conjugate. In fact g=(234) satisfies g a g^(-1)=b.
These give explicit K-conjugators at every endpoint. To compare
different occurrences of one actual Ti, first transport along the
actual F-conjugators from D74. Since the map
  gamma0:E->B, gamma0(e)=(a^{u(e)},phi(e))                    (D5)
is a continuous global lift of phi and u is zero on those F-conjugators,
this transport has first component one. Its second component makes
the source labels agree by the actual equality in E. The preceding
identity or g in K then aligns each endpoint image with gamma0(t_i).
Thus all three full section classes admit simultaneously compatible
local lifts up to K-conjugacy in this precise finite problem.

Nevertheless no continuous gamma:E->B can satisfy pi gamma=phi and
  gamma|Dj = k_j sigma_j(-) k_j^(-1), with k_j in K,
for all three j. Suppose such gamma exists and let beta=pr_A5 gamma.
The images X=beta(x), Y=beta(y) have order two. The original equality
z=(xy)^(-1) and (D3) force XY to have order three. The group
  Q=<X,Y>=beta(F)
has order six. It is normal in beta(E), since F is normal in E.
Consequently S=beta(s) belongs to N_A5(Q). Moreover alpha(x)=x^(-1)
implies that S centralizes X. For every such ordered pair (X,Y),
  N_A5(Q)=Q and C_{N_A5(Q)}(X)={1,X}.                         (D6)
These are exact finite equalities, verified exhaustively below. They
also follow from the usual faithful action of Q on its three-point
orbit and its complementary two-point orbit: a normalizer preserves
those distinct orbit sizes, whose set stabilizer in A5 is Q; the
centralizer of a reflection in Q of order six is that reflection's
order-two subgroup.

On the other hand the Dx condition requires (X,S) to be simultaneously
conjugate in A5 to (R,a). Here a is nonidentity and a is different from
R. Thus S is neither 1 nor X, contradicting (D6).

This proof uses the actual original generators x,y,z, actual quotient
(D2), actual normal subgroup F, and actual alpha(x)=x^(-1). It does
not insert a hypothetical standard presentation of E. It proves that
the particular class-compatible local maps (D4) fail to have a global
lift even though all their local projections are injective. Its role
is to rule out promoting the proved section lifting property to this
stronger unrestricted peripheral lifting property. No assertion is
made that the specific peripheral choices needed in D74.40 encounter
this obstruction. The same proof applies at f=h=1, where the explicit
standard isomorphism E=C2(s)*C2(xs)*C2(ys) is available. Its obstruction
therefore concerns the stated universal local-lifting requirement,
including in that standard model.

Executed finite evidence for D.2:
The same code and outputs contain the full A5 computation. It lists
all sixty elements and all fifteen involutions, verifies each local
dihedral relation, retains explicit endpoint conjugators, and exhausts
all sixty ordered involution pairs (X,Y) whose product has order three.
For every pair it computes Q, its normalizer and the indicated
centralizer; none permits S. It also verifies the eleven local graph

reflection's vector is (1,0) modulo two, so these nine cases exhaust

## Cocompact actual-operator sphere fillings

C.90 research and proof record

Result proved
For the actual C.81 data with compact quotient N=O/Q, every positive based
homotopy group of the original boundary-fixed centralizer vanishes. This
includes the original compactification, all individual Q labels, maps and
inverses, and nonorientable quotients. No extension of a coordinate change
or of q to the original circle is used.

Exact proof route
The one-orbit evaluation bundle from C.81 identifies the positive homotopy
groups with those of the subgroup fixing one specified x over p. A based
sphere in that subgroup descends to the pointed quotient identity component.
The quotient is closed and aspherical because its universal cover is O.
Yagasaki's Lemma2.1(i), with fixed set {p}, gives a contractible quotient
identity component. Its full exception list excludes this pair: sphere and
projective plane have nonzero pi2, while the torus and Klein-bottle exceptions
have empty fixed set. The exact item used is (i), not (ii).

Normalize a chosen contraction using J_r(b)=C_{1-r}(b)C_{1-r}(1)^{-1}.
Lift J_r(b_xi) through the original covering from identity. Independently
lifting the inverse family and using uniqueness proves the inverse equations.
The same uniqueness retains every Q label. The track of the fixed lift x
stays in its discrete fiber; it is constant. This proves that the final lift
equals the original a_xi, since both lifts fix x. The sphere basepoint stays
identity. Finally C.88's exact compact-family extension criterion applies
with K=N and empty tail. The resulting original closed-disk family provides
the required filling, and the C.81 based homotopy carries it back to the
arbitrary original sphere.

===================================================================

Completed assertion
-------------------
For either actual inclusion mathcal K <= R <= V, take any continuous
rho:V -> Aff_1(k), where k is any finite field of characteristic p.
Write M=rho(mathcal K), N=rho(R), D=chi(V), C=chi(R), and identify the
translation intersection M intersect T_k with an additive subgroup U
of k. Put k0=F_p(D) and k1=F_p(C).

The proof establishes that U is always k1-linear. It proves M=N for
the exact class in which U is k0-linear. Therefore M=N whenever C=1
or k0=k1. In particular it proves the full equality for every map
V -> Aff_1(F_p), for every prime p. There is no translation-intersection
restriction in that prime-field corollary. Characteristics two and
three are included.

Exact constructions in the proof
--------------------------------
The actual map D+ -> R from F22 transports F21 normal generation;
then rho|R and the scalar projection give normal_N(M)=N and chi(K)=C.
For C=1, N is abelian and the equality follows immediately.

For C nontrivial, conjugation by an actual element (b,c) of M sends
the translation u to cu. This proves C-stability and k1-linearity of U.
The proof gives the elementary finite-field argument that C is cyclic.
Choose its generator c and an actual lift m=(b,c) in M. The point
z=b/(1-c) is fixed by m. Conjugation by the explicitly specified
translation tau_z puts m at (0,c), leaves U literally unchanged, and
gives the exact group M_z=U semidirect C with both coordinate maps.
This constructs the complement used in the argument inside the actual
marginal image.

When U is k0-linear, every k0-linear map ell:k -> k0 vanishing on U
makes ell(d_z) an actual continuous chi-crossed homomorphism, since
chi(V) lies in k0. It vanishes on mathcal K. F24 injectivity over k0
therefore makes it zero on V. Extending a basis of U shows that the
intersection of the kernels of these exact coefficient maps is U.
Hence d_z(V) lies in U, and N_z lies in U semidirect C=M_z. The
reverse inclusion is the original subgroup inclusion. The inverse
translation conjugation gives M=N.

The field equality k1=k0 supplies the needed k0-linearity by the
already proved C-stability. This is the exact transfer used for
the stated scalar-field class; it is not presumed for other images.

## Original-metric exhaustion estimate and exact failed transfer

Original-topology obstruction to the compact-open exhaustion estimate

This is a record of one exact failed transfer in the noncompact C.12
attack. It is not a claimed obstruction to a contraction of the original
group: C.87 already contracts the entire radial group used below.

Retain C.84's original j:R2 -> Int D, j(z)=z/(1+|z|), and the individual
operator T(x,y)=(x+1,y). Its quotient is N=(R/Z)xR. The extended plane
translations give the actual transitive boundary-fixed commuting group,
so C.81 and C.88 apply to precisely this disk and covering.

For an integer m>=1 put R=m+1 and K_m=(R/Z)x[-m,m]. Define
  beta(u)=max(0,1-4|u|),
  F_(R,t)(x,y)=(x+t R beta(y-R),y),  0<=t<=1.
The inverse subtracts the same t R beta(y-R), since y is unchanged.
Thus each F_(R,t) is a homeomorphism, and the same formula proves
F_(R,t) T^q=T^q F_(R,t) for every integer q. Both map and inverse are
continuous in (t,x,y). Their quotient supports lie in
(R/Z)x[R-1/4,R+1/4], disjoint from K_m. The whole path fixes K_m,
starts at identity and ends at F_(R,1).

For fixed R, the Euclidean displacement of both map and inverse is at
most R, uniformly over t. As |z| tends to infinity, bounded displacement
makes both the radial length and direction of j(F_(R,t)(z)) converge
uniformly in t to those of j(z). Consequently h_(R,t)=j F_(R,t) j^{-1},
extended by identity on S1, is a continuous path in the original
closed-disk centralizer, including maps and inverses. It belongs to
the identity path component of the original stabilizer of pi^{-1}(K_m).

At z=(0,R), beta(0)=1, so F_(R,1)(z)=(R,R). The horizontal coordinates
of their radial images are respectively0 and R/(1+sqrt(2)R). Thus
  sup_(w in D) |h_(R,1)(w)-w| >= R/(1+sqrt(2)R) > 2/5.
The last inequality holds for every real R>=1. Set R=1+s with s>=0.
Then 5R-2=3+5s>0 and
  (5R-2)^2-8R^2 = 1+14s+17s^2 >0.
Squaring against the positive 2sqrt(2)R gives
5R-2>2sqrt(2)R, which is exactly the asserted bound.

It follows that the diameters of these actual stabilizers, even their
identity path components, do not tend to zero for the original uniform
disk metric as the compact quotient cores K_m exhaust N. In contrast,
the same sequence of descended maps and inverses converges to identity
on every compact subset of N, because its supports eventually avoid
that subset. The lift fixing any specified point over K_1 is precisely
the displayed F_(R,1). This gives the exact map and sequence witnessing
the failure of inverse continuity from this compact-open quotient
subspace to the original disk topology.

of Proposition4.1(1), printedpages11-12, constructs a contraction by
successively fixing compact cores. Its metric is the ordinary weighted

This result gives an exact presentation of the full D+ in the original
F19 configuration coordinates. It also identifies the exact source map
whose image is K+. The surjectivity of that source map is still open.

Based sections and actual inverse coordinates
--------------------------------------------
The old finite points are 0,1,v_zeta and the four other v_u. The two
moving basepoints are p=a(s0) and n=-a(s0). Choose an embedded tree
joining the seven old points and p while avoiding n; a small regular
neighborhood is a disk B containing those eight points and excluding n.
The inclusion of B minus the seven old points into the corresponding
punctured plane induces an isomorphism on pi1 at p. The same holds after
filling the four old v_u. Inside B the actual map z -> (z,n) gives a
section of the positive-point forgetting. The two disk inclusions and
these two point maps commute with the actual puncture filling, so their
induced group sections commute too. All basepoints are the original
(p,n); the comparison paths to F19 are constant.

The F19 full-topology argument gives the actual full split rows
  J = V semidirect V+ -> J4 = P semidirect Q+,
where V=Fhat8 is the negative-point fiber, V+=Fhat7 is the positive
point group, P=Fhat4 and Q+=Fhat3. The two filling maps kill precisely
the four old v_u meridians. Put R1=ker(V->P), R+=ker(V+->Q+).
Then D+ is exactly R1 semidirect R+, under
  (b,g) -> iota(b)*sigma(g),
with inverse
  d -> (iota^{-1}(d*sigma(p_+d)^{-1}), p_+d).
The action is conjugation by this actual section sigma.

The geometric action has a complete free-word recipe
----------------------------------------------------
In a retained labelled disk chart, the three retained old points occupy
positions 1,2,3; the four filled old points occupy 4,5,6,7; the positive
point occupies 8; the negative point is the exterior basepoint. Moving
the positive point around old position i gives
  beta_i=sigma_7 ... sigma_(i+1) sigma_i^2
                         sigma_(i+1)^-1 ... sigma_7^-1.
Its action on the eight-generator fiber is the exact Artin substitution
of this word. The proof ties this to actual point pushing using the
same erased-conjugator coordinate u=w^-1 as F20. Its images on the
geometric kernel basis are
  tau_i=X8^-1 ... X(i+1)^-1 Xi^-1 X(i+1) ... X8.
This triangular substitution is its own inverse. It identifies the
actual fiber with the chosen Artin coordinates and commutes with both
fillings. The normalized moduli comparison uses the same explicit
affine-coordinate isomorphism as F20, with constant first two old
coordinates; there is no replacement of an ambient group without a map.

The compact generator topology is retained
------------------------------------------
For a profinite space T, F_c(T) is constructed from the abstract free
group on its underlying set using only finite quotient maps for which
T->finite group is continuous. Its inverse limit has the universal
property for continuous maps from T to profinite groups.

For a finitely generated free profinite Q and a finite set I, left
translation on Q times I gives a jointly continuous action on F_c(QxI).
Every continuous finite-valued map on QxI factors through Q/N times I
for some open normal N. Its translates have finite orbit; intersecting
the finitely many translated quotient kernels gives invariant open
subgroups refining every quotient. These prove the required joint
continuity, not merely pointwise continuity of automorphisms.

The exact inverse maps are
  Fhat(Q-basis, v_j) -> F_c(QxI) semidirect Q,
      x -> (1,x), v_j -> (e(1,j),1),
and
  e(q,j) -> s(q)*v_j*s(q)^-1, q -> s(q).
Both composites fix all displayed generators and therefore are the
identity. Their projections to Q are the actual filling retractions.
This proves
  R+ = F_c(Q+ x four old labels),
  R1 = F_c(P x four old labels),
with the explicit conjugate-generator maps. No full completion of an
infinitely generated discrete kernel is used.

The full action on arbitrary compact generators is determined by the
seven Artin words: e(q,j) in R+ acts as
alpha_s(q) alpha_u_j alpha_s(q)^-1 on V. Apply that automorphism to
s1(v)*U_k*s1(v)^-1 and then apply the inverse compact-generator map.
This is a continuous formula in both profinite indices q and v.

What both one-point projections retain
--------------------------------------
The opposite forgetting p_- fills the positive puncture t on V and
kills the image of sigma, since that section fixes the negative point.
Thus on the actual D+ coordinates,
  (p_+,p_-)(b,g)=(g,h(b)),
where h kills t. Its restriction R1->R- is onto by retaining the other
seven free letters. Hence D+ -> R+ times R- is onto, and its kernel is
  W=ker(V->P) intersect ker(V->V_-).

Retain Q-=Fhat(X1,X2,X3) in V and let eta(q,e)=s(q)*e*s(q)^-1.
The kernel V->Q- is the free profinite group on the disjoint compact
union Q- times {U1,...,U4} and Q- times {t}. By the universal property
it is the free profinite product A coproduct B of the two corresponding
free compact-generator groups. The two fillings are its two actual
factor retractions, so W is exactly the kernel to A times B.
Quotienting by all [eta(q,U_j),eta(q',t)] makes the two factor images
commute. Multiplication from A times B and the two retractions give
inverse maps; this proves the exact closed normal closure description.
The displayed generator set is invariant under Q- translation, so the
same normal closure taken in V gives W.

The concrete element [U1,t] belongs to W. Send U1 to I+E12, t to
I+E23 and the other letters to identity in UT3(Z/m). The commutator
is I+E13, and its profinite power z has image I+(z mod m)E13.
The formula holds for every modulus and detects every nonzero z in
Zhat, so the element generates a full closed Zhat. This records an
actual interaction subgroup killed by both one-point projections;
it does not assert that this element is outside or inside K+.

The exact remaining source map
------------------------------
F17-F19 give the actual free source basis: eleven retained old
meridians and sixteen additional collision meridians m_d. Applying
the compact-generator inverse construction to this source filling
identifies its kernel with F_c(L times Delta), with
  (l,d) -> i(l)*m_d*i(l)^-1.
Its image under Phi-dagger is the continuous homomorphism
  Lambda(l,d)=j(l)*nu_d*j(l)^-1
into D+. The exact source row of F19 gives image(Lambda)=K+.
For z=Lambda(l,d), its actual presentation coordinates are
  g=p_+(z), b=iota^{-1}(z*sigma(g)^-1).
The original source section j and the independently constructed
point-pushing section sigma both occur in this formula with their
actual maps. Their images have not been identified. The equality
K+=D+ is therefore the surjectivity of this specified Lambda onto
the proved semidirect product; that last surjectivity is not proved.

The two marginal images have an exact product comparison
--------------------------------------------------------
Partition Delta into the eight positive and eight negative collisions.
Let Y^+ fill the negative collisions and Y^- fill the positive collisions.
Their completed groups L_+ and L_- are Fhat19, and the maps q_+ and q_-
to L=Fhat11 kill exactly their respective eight extra meridians. The
actual one-point source maps Phi_+ and Phi_- factor the full nine-point
forgettings and have
  mathcal K_+=p_+(K+)=Phi_+(ker q_+),
  mathcal K_-=p_-(K+)=Phi_-(ker q_-).
These are retained actual images; their fullness in R_+ and R_- is open.

For a positive collision meridian, forgetting the positive point removes
the collision, so its image under the full opposite forgetting is the
identity. The negative collision statement is the corresponding one.
These killed-coordinate identities persist under conjugation by j(l)
using the actual full forgetting maps on G. This step does not apply
p_+ or p_- to j(l) when j(l) lies outside J.

The compact image of F_c(L times Delta_+) inside K+ therefore has joint
image mathcal K_+ times {1}; the negative signed image has joint image
{1} times mathcal K_-. Lift an arbitrary pair separately to those two
compact source images and multiply the two lifts in K+. Their product
maps to the given pair. Consequently the source row
  1 -> K+ intersect W -> K+ -> mathcal K_+ times mathcal K_- -> 1
is exact and maps by actual inclusions to the proved D+ row
  1 -> W -> D+ -> R_+ times R_- -> 1.
No joint correlation remains beyond the individual marginal images;
the argument does not identify either marginal with its whole target.
