## Original discrete-operator carrier and radial-topology continuation

CONTINUATION AUDIT AFTER C81-C83
Unregistered research note. Previously accepted fragments are unchanged.
All assertions called proved below have their maps and proofs in this note.
No general family-to-skeleton deformation is asserted.

1. Q-NATURAL FILLED CARRIERS AND SIMPLY CONNECTED BALL COMPONENTS

Use the actual unit disk Dbar with its Euclidean distance d, its interior
O, the original free proper operator action Q, and C81's compatible
invariant metric d_Q(x,y)=sup_(q in Q)d(qx,qy).

For compact K subset O, let Fill(K) be K together with the bounded
components of its complement in the ambient Euclidean plane. Since K
lies in the convex open disk O, Fill(K) is compact in O. Equivalently,
it is O minus the unique component of O\K whose closure is not compact
in O. Uniqueness follows from the circle collar outside a compact
Euclidean subdisk containing K; every other complementary component
lies in the compact convex hull of K.

For each actual q in Q, homeomorphism invariance of compactness and of
complementary components therefore proves the exact equation

       q Fill(K) = Fill(qK).

No extension of q to the original circle is used. Also Fill(K) is
contained in the Euclidean convex hull of K: any point outside that
convex hull has a separating line and hence a path to infinity in
the complement of K.

Let K be compact inside B_(d_Q)(x,r). Compatibility of d_Q gives
s=max_(k in K)d_Q(x,k)<r. For every q, the compact set qK lies in
the closed Euclidean ball centered at qx of radius s. Its filled
hull lies there by convexity. Consequently

       Fill(K) subset {z:d_Q(x,z)<=s} subset B_(d_Q)(x,r).

Every component C of B_(d_Q)(x,r) is simply connected. To see this,
put an arbitrary loop in C inside the interior of a compact connected
polygonal planar surface W subset C. Such a W is obtained from a
finite cover of its compact image by small disks inside C, joined
within C and replaced by a finite polygonal regular neighborhood.
Filling W's finitely many holes gives a closed topological disk.
The preceding estimate puts that entire fill inside the same ball;
it is connected and meets C, hence lies in C. The loop is null
there, with its basepoint retained. This also supplies a compact
disk carrier for each individual filling.

This statement controls individual carrier sets. It gives no
continuous choice over all centers or all families, and no ambient
equivariant lift of those fillings.

2. SMALL CARRIERS CAN HAVE LARGE CONNECTED SATURATION

Retain C83's literal radial coordinate
j(z)=z/(1+norm(z)), its inverse w/(1-norm(w)), and
Q=<j T_(1,0) j^(-1)>.
For n>=2 let K_n be the closed Euclidean radius-one disk in the
plane centered at (0,n^2), transported by j to O.

For z,w in the original planar radius-one disk and each integer m,
the C83 radial estimate gives

 |j(z+(m,0))-j(w+(m,0))|
 <=2|z-w|/(1+|w+(m,0)|)
 <=4/n^2.

Indeed the last planar norm is at least n^2-1. Hence
diam_(d_Q)(K_n)<=4/n^2.

The disks translated by consecutive integers overlap, so their
union is connected. It contains the full horizontal line y=n^2:
every real x is within 1/2 of an integer disk center. The radial
image of this line has limit points (-1,0) and (1,0). Its diameter
has supremum 2. Thus

       diam_d(union_(q in Q) qK_n)=2

while diam_(d_Q)(K_n) tends to zero. These carriers are compact
disks, so filling them does not change the calculation. The setup
retains C81's transitive actual boundary-fixed translation subgroup.

Therefore a displacement estimate for a proposed lift cannot be
deduced merely by bounding the diameter of this saturated support.
This example does not rule out a controlled trajectory construction
inside the overlapping saturation.

3. THE LITERAL FABEL PATH AND THE ACTUAL Q-LABEL EQUATIONS

Primary source inspected:
Paul Fabel, Isotopies of planar compacta need not extend to isotopies
of planar continua, arXiv:math/0202163v1:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0202163
Corollary 7 and its displayed construction are on printed pages 5-6.
The construction uses the convergent sequence {0,1,1/2,1/3,...};
on each active interval one label circles its neighbor while every
other label stays fixed. This note imports no conclusion from that
construction for an operator action.

Here is the exact comparison. For an actual Q-equivariant labelled
configuration path, indexed by a Q-invariant set V, the equations are

       z_(qv)(t)=q z_v(t),       z_v(0)=v.

Since q is injective,
z_v(t) differs from v exactly when z_(qv)(t) differs from qv.
Thus the set of moved labels at every time is Q-invariant. A free
infinite Q-action has only infinite orbits, so a nonempty finite set
of moved labels cannot occur. In particular, the literal Fabel
one-moving-label intervals cannot satisfy these equations on even
one, or on finitely many, actual free infinite Q-orbits.

This is a direct obstruction to assigning the required labels to
that path. It does not assert that no modification of the example
could ever interact with an operator action. No such modified
example has been constructed in this work.

4. EXACT SUBLINEAR DESCRIPTION IN THE RADIAL TRANSLATION MODEL

Again fix exactly C83's radial disk and Q, and write a plane
homeomorphism commuting with T_(1,0) as

       F(x,y)=(X(x,y),Y(x,y))
             =(x+u(x,y), y+w(x,y)).

Both u and w are periodic of period one in x. Let C_rad be the
actual original-disk centralizer, conjugated to plane maps using j.
Then F belongs to C_rad exactly when

       lim_(R->infinity)
       sup_(0<=x<=1, |y|>=R)
       norm(F(x,y)-(x,y))/|y| = 0.                 (A)

Its inverse satisfies the same condition. No coordinate is changed
after this choice of j.

Proof of necessity, including compact families.
Let F_i range in a compact family of actual boundary-fixed maps.
Suppose |y_i| tends to infinity and 0<=x_i<=1. Choose integers
m_i^+,m_i^- with

       x_i+m_i^+ = y_i+e_i^+,
       x_i+m_i^- = -y_i+e_i^-,
       |e_i^+|,|e_i^-|<=1/2.

After a subsequence sign(y_i) is constant. The two radial input
points converge to the two corresponding diagonal boundary
directions. Compactness of the actual family and pointwise fixation
of the original circle force the same two output limits. Periodicity
keeps the two output second coordinates equal to Y_i=Y_Fi(x_i,y_i).
It follows that

       (X_Fi(x_i,y_i)+m_i^+)/Y_i -> 1,
       (X_Fi(x_i,y_i)+m_i^-)/Y_i -> -1.

The ratios are defined eventually because the limiting boundary
directions have nonzero second coordinate. Subtraction gives
(m_i^+-m_i^-)/Y_i ->2. Since
(m_i^+-m_i^-)/y_i ->2, we get Y_i/y_i ->1.
Either ratio then gives u_Fi(x_i,y_i)/y_i ->0.
Thus (A) holds uniformly for every compact actual family. Applying
this to the compact family of inverses gives the inverse assertion.

Proof of sufficiency.
For any epsilon>0, (A) gives displacement <=epsilon |y| when
|y|>=R, uniformly in all x by periodicity. For |y|<=R, periodicity
and compactness bound displacement by a finite M_R. Consequently
norm(F(z)-z)/(1+norm(z)) tends to zero as norm(z) tends to infinity.
The explicit radial estimate C83.3 gives
norm(jF(z)-j(z)) tending uniformly to zero. The map jFj^(-1)
therefore extends continuously by the identity to the original
circle. It is a continuous bijection of the compact closed disk,
so its inverse is continuous. Necessity applied to that inverse
proves its version of (A).

The topology also has an exact metric description. Put

 ||F-H||_* =
 sup_(0<=x<=1, y in R)
 norm(F(x,y)-H(x,y))/(1+|y|),

 and delta_*(F,H)=||F-H||_*+||F^(-1)-H^(-1)||_*.

This is finite on C_rad and gives precisely the original disk
map-and-inverse topology under j.

For the forward implication, a convergent sequence together with
its limit is a compact actual family. The uniform form of (A)
controls its weighted tails, and actual convergence gives ordinary
coordinate convergence on [0,1] times every compact y-interval.
These two facts give convergence in ||.||_*; repeat for inverses.

Conversely, for a fixed H in C_rad the number

       c_H=sup_(x,y) (1+|y|)/(1+norm(H(x,y)))

is finite. At large |y|, (A) implies |Y_H(x,y)|>=|y|/2;
on the remaining y-band the numerator is bounded. The radial
estimate with basepoint H(x,y) consequently gives

       sup_z |jF(z)-jH(z)| <= 2c_H ||F-H||_*.

The inverse version gives the other term of the original disk
metric. This proves both continuous inverse topology maps.

5. AN EXPLICIT CONTRACTIBLE SUBSPACE WITH BOTH ACTUAL CONTROLS

Let M be the subspace of C_rad consisting of the F for which,
for every real x, y |-> Y_F(x,y) is an increasing homeomorphism
of R. The following is an actual contraction of all of M,
fixing the identity; it preserves the original Q labels.

Define

       V_F(x,y)=(x,Y_F(x,y)),
       H_F=F V_F^(-1).

Each V_F is a plane homeomorphism. Its inverse is jointly continuous:
at a converging sequence of parameters x and target values, monotonicity
and two bracketing y-values bound the inverse, and any convergent
subsequence must solve the same strictly monotone equation.
Periodicity gives V_F T_(1,0)=T_(1,0) V_F.
Condition (A) for V_F follows from that for F; hence V_F is an
actual element of C_rad. Thus H_F is also in C_rad, and it has
the form

       H_F(x,y)=(h_F,y(x),y),
       h_F,y(x+1)=h_F,y(x)+1,

with each h_F,y an increasing homeomorphism of R.
The inverse equations show that F=H_F V_F exactly.

For 0<=r<=1 put

       V_F,r(x,y)=(x,(1-r)y+rY_F(x,y)),
       H_F,r(x,y)=((1-r)x+r h_F,y(x),y),
       A_r(F)=H_F,r V_F,r.

The convex combinations are strictly increasing and proper on
their indicated real fibers; the displayed periodicity is unchanged.
They are plane homeomorphisms commuting with the original translation.
Their displacements are scalar multiples of the original respective
fiber displacements, so (A) holds uniformly for r in [0,1].
They therefore extend by the identity to the original circle.
The second coordinate of A_r(F) is the increasing function
(1-r)y+rY_F(x,y), so A_r(F) remains in M.
The faces are A_0(F)=identity, A_1(F)=F, A_r(identity)=identity.

Here are the actual parameter-topology checks. F |-> V_F is continuous
in weighted forward displacement, by the formula. The preceding
radial bound makes its disk extensions continuous in uniform forward
distance. On a compact space, uniform convergence to a homeomorphism
implies uniform convergence of inverses:

 sup |A_n^(-1)-A^(-1)|
 <= omega_(A^(-1))(sup |A_n-A|),

where omega_(A^(-1)) is a modulus of continuity of the fixed inverse.
Consequently F |-> V_F is continuous in the actual group topology.
The group operations then make F |-> H_F continuous.
For the interpolation, weighted forward differences are bounded by
r||F-H||_*+|r-s| ||H-identity||_* on either fiber subgroup.
The same radial bound and compact inverse argument give joint
continuity in (r,F) for both interpolated factors. Their product
therefore gives the asserted actual contraction, including the
inverse topology. This contracts based compact families lying
in M with every original boundary and Q label retained.

The inclusion M subset C_rad has not been replaced by an equality.
For an explicit map outside M, choose mutually disjoint Euclidean
disks of radius 1/10 centered at (k+1/2,0), k in Z, and rotate each
through angle pi on its radius-1/20 core, tapering the angle
continuously to zero at the radius-1/10 boundary. Use identical
radial formulas on all integer translates and the identity elsewhere.
This is a bounded-displacement Q-commuting plane homeomorphism, so
it belongs to C_rad. On the vertical line through a core center,
its second coordinate reverses the order of the two nearby points.
It therefore lies outside M.

The unresolved step in this model is a controlled deformation of
an arbitrary original family into M, or another explicit contracting
subspace, while retaining the weighted topology (equivalently the
original map-and-inverse topology). No such deformation is supplied
by the coordinate characterization or by the contraction above.

A. Exact correspondence between the two D75 reflection labels
-------------------------------------------------------------
Retain the original F, c, v, the unique g with g v g^{-1}=c v, and
  a_(mu,0)=c^((mu-1)/2) g,
  a_(mu,1)=c^((mu+1)/2) g^{-1}
from D75. For i=0,1 define the actual compact solution space
  T_i = {(mu,k) in Zhat^times times F:
          k (c^(-mu) a_(mu,i)) k^{-1} = a_(mu,i)}.
The profinite exponent maps, group operations, and equality relation make
these closed subspaces of the indicated compact product.

There are explicit mutually inverse continuous maps
  Phi: T_1 -> T_0,
       (mu,k) -> (-mu, c^(-(mu+1)/2) k g),
  Psi: T_0 -> T_1,
       (nu,l) -> (-nu, c^((1-nu)/2) l g^{-1}).
All half-exponents are the same full Zhat half-exponents as in D75.
In particular the original c is retained in both source and target equations.

Proof of the maps. Put d=(mu+1)/2 and b=a_(-mu,0)=c^(-d)g. Then
  a_(mu,1)=c^d b^{-1} c^{-d}.
Conjugating the T_1 equation by c^{-d}, and setting k'=c^{-d}kc^d,
gives
  k' c^{-mu} b^{-1} k'^{-1}=b^{-1}.
Taking inverses gives k' b c^mu k'^{-1}=b. Set l=k'b=c^{-d}kg.
The literal product calculation
  l(c^mu b)l^{-1}
     =k'b(c^mu b)b^{-1}k'^{-1}
     =k'b c^mu k'^{-1}
     =b
is exactly the T_0 equation with multiplier nu=-mu.
All operations reverse: from this T_0 equation, put k'=l b^{-1},
take inverses and conjugate by c^d. The resulting k is
  c^d k' c^{-d}=c^d l g^{-1}.
This is exactly Psi, and substitution in the two formulas proves both
composites are the identity. Their continuity follows from the actual
continuous group and exponent operations.

Thus both labelled solution spaces are related by these explicit maps.
The D75 existence question is precisely nonemptiness of T_0 (and equally
of T_1). This calculation establishes no nonemptiness assertion. It also
does not alter the two model maps or the full outside-centralizer/root
constructions already given in D75.23--26.

### C.83: a continuous infinite evaluation loop with no original-disk lift

The example specifies the actual compactification, operator group, transitive commuting group, vertex labels and both topologies. Its plane coordinate is the homeomorphism

\[
j(z)=\frac{z}{1+\lVert z\rVert},\qquad
j^{-1}(w)=\frac{w}{1-\lVert w\rVert}
\]

from the plane to the interior of the original closed unit disk. The operator group is the conjugate through this map of integer horizontal translations. It is closed, discrete, free and proper on the interior. All plane translations extend through this same compactification by the identity on the original circle, and provide the actual transitive commuting subgroup required by C.81. The quantitative extension estimate is

\[
\lVert j(z+v)-j(z)\rVert\le
\frac{2\lVert v\rVert}{1+\lVert z\rVert}.
\]

It controls the maps and their inverses, jointly over compact translation-parameter sets.

The invariant grid has labelled vertices \((k/4,l)\), indexed by a fixed enumeration of \(\mathbb Z^2\). The generator of the operator group acts by the literal label change \((k,l)\mapsto(k+4,l)\). Dividing each rectangle by the same diagonal gives a quotient triangulation. Each closed lifted vertex star has horizontal width \(1/2<1\), so it projects injectively under the unit deck translation. The stars have a common diameter bound in the plane. The displayed radial estimate makes their original-disk diameters tend to zero as the vertices escape, proving the finite-large-star property of C.82 for this exact carrier.

The target is the actual simultaneous evaluation image, with the subspace topology of ordered-coordinate convergence and vague convergence of its counting measures. The evaluation map from the original disk group is continuous: coordinate convergence follows from uniform convergence of maps; for any compactly supported test function, uniform convergence of inverse maps confines all relevant original vertices to one compact interior neighborhood. Thus the test-function sum eventually involves a fixed finite set of labels. This proves continuity of the actual map in both components of the specified target topology.

Put \(b(u)=\max(0,1-4|u|)\). The explicit shear family

\[
F_{n,s}(x,y)=(x+sn\,b(y-n),y),\qquad 0\le s\le1
\]

has inverse with the minus sign and commutes with every integer horizontal translation. For each fixed \(n\), its displacement is bounded by \(n\); the radial estimate therefore gives an actual continuous family of boundary-fixed disk homeomorphisms, including its inverses. Only the grid row \(l=n\) moves.

On the interval \([2^{-n-1},2^{-n}]\), the amplitude rises linearly from zero to one and returns to zero. Concatenate these evaluated paths as the intervals accumulate at zero. Every fixed finite set of labels is eventually fixed. Every compact planar test support eventually misses the moving row and all its images, since the shear preserves the second coordinate. These two exact facts prove continuity of the concatenated loop in the stated evaluation-image topology. Multiplying all amplitudes by \(1-r\), for \(0\le r\le1\), gives an explicit based null-homotopy in that same image; the continuity estimates are uniform in \(r\).

At the peak time \(t_n=3\,2^{-n-2}\), every putative lift must send the vertex \(j(0,n)\) to \(j(n,n)\). Its uniform original-disk displacement is consequently at least

\[
\lVert j(n,n)-j(0,n)\rVert
\ge\frac{n}{1+\sqrt2\,n}>\frac13.
\]

Since \(t_n\to0\), no lift starting at the identity is continuous. The bound applies to every homeomorphism with the required labelled evaluation, regardless of its behavior between vertices. It proves failure of path lifting and hence of the Serre and Hurewicz fibration properties for this exact evaluation map. The target loop is explicitly null-homotopic. No nonzero homotopy class in the original centralizer is claimed.

### F.21: transitivity on the full divisor cosets and normal generation in the joint kernel

F.20 had proved transitivity on its specified finite quotient families. F.21 proves the actual source action transitive on each entire discrete cross-divisor coset space, and then on the corresponding full profinite coset space. It retains all four old labels, both new-point signs and the original chosen source meridians and whiskers.

For each old label \(u\in\mu_5\setminus\{\zeta\}\), the coordinates are

\[
A(s)=\frac{\zeta-s}{\zeta+s},\quad
C_u(s)=\frac{u-s}{u+s},\quad
B=A^2,\quad U=C_u^2,\quad V=\epsilon A.
\]

The argument is based first at the actual selected collision point \(d\) in the filled source \(Y\). At that point \(U=V\), giving a literal common diagonal basepoint. The original source whisker and its image in the configuration space transport every group and forgetting map back to the original basepoint. The selected meridian is retained through these specified transports.

The fourfold square-root cover of \(\mathcal M_{0,5}\) is

\[
W=\{(A,C):A,C\notin\{0,\infty,1,-1\},\ C\ne\pm A\}.
\]

It maps through the intermediate double cover \(W_A\) by \((A,C)\mapsto(A,C^2)\). The actual pencil

\[
\kappa(A,C)=\frac{C-A}{1-AC}
\]

takes values in \(\mathscr B=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,-1\}\). Removing \(E=\{AC=1\}\) gives a locally trivial bundle over \(\mathscr B\setminus\{\infty\}\). Its fiber is the sphere with the eight specified punctures \(0,\infty,1,-1,-k,-1/k\) and the two roots of \(kA^2+2A+k=0\). Their distinctness, local root choices and disjoint puncture isotopies provide explicit bundle charts.

The old source lies on the fiber \(k_u=(u-\zeta)/(u+\zeta)\). In its original \(s\)-coordinate that entire fiber removes exactly \(0,\infty,\pm\zeta,\pm u,\pm t_u\), where \(t_u^2=\zeta u\). The map from \(Y\) fills the remaining four punctures, so its fundamental-group map onto the fiber image is onto. The divisor \(E\) is connected and smooth, and the derivative of \(1/\kappa\) transverse to it is nonzero. Filling it kills exactly the normal closure of its meridian, whose base image is one meridian of infinity. The resulting actual quotient maps prove

\[
N=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\pi_1(Y,d)\to J=\pi_1(W)\bigr)
 =\ker\bigl(\kappa_*:J\to\pi_1(\mathscr B,k_u)\bigr).
\]

This is a discrete equality; the subsequent proof does not require exactness after completing this pencil-kernel sequence.

The new section of \(W_A\) is \(A\mapsto(A,\epsilon A)\). Its pullback to \(W\) is the connected double cover \(r\mapsto\epsilon r^2\) on the sphere minus \(0,\infty,\pm1,\pm i\), with the literal map \(r\mapsto(\epsilon r^2,r)\). The pencil on this pullback is

\[
f_\epsilon(r)=\frac{r}{r^2+\epsilon r+1}.
\]

Deleting the extra target branch value \(\epsilon/3\) makes it an unramified degree-two cover. The meridian of that value has odd covering monodromy and is killed by the actual target filling. Multiplying a base element by that meridian to the negative of its parity proves that the cover subgroup maps onto the filled-base fundamental group.

Writing \(T=\pi_1(W_A)\) and \(M\) for the new-section subgroup, the precise factorizations are

\[
J=N(M\cap J),\qquad T=NM.
\]

The diagonal right-coset coordinate is \((b_o,b_n)\operatorname{diag}\mapsto b_nb_o^{-1}\), with inverse \(v\mapsto(1,v)\operatorname{diag}\). In this coordinate the actual source acts by \(v\mapsto m(a(n))vn^{-1}\). Factor \(v^{-1}=nm\) in \(T=NM\) and project to the \(A\)-coordinate. This forces \(m=m(a(n))^{-1}\), so \(v\) is the image of the identity under the source action. It proves discrete transitivity. The full completion comparison already proved in F.19–F.20 identifies the full divisor coset with \(\widehat F_3\). The compact source orbit contains the dense discrete orbit and is therefore the whole coset space.

A small oriented normal circle bundle over the regular part of each cross divisor gives actual lifts of its loops that centralize the selected meridian. Its base projection is onto on fundamental groups, its fiber generator is central, and the simple holomorphic source collision identifies that generator with the original positive primitive meridian. Completing this homomorphism gives a compact centralizing image whose projection contains the full divisor subgroup; injectivity of the circle-bundle completion is not required.

Let \(N_D\) be the closed normal closure of \(K^+\) inside \(D^+\). Source transitivity and the centralizer lift factor every ambient element as \(g=dhc\), where \(d\in D^+\), \(h\) lies in the actual drilled source image and \(c\) centralizes the chosen meridian \(\nu\). Hence

\[
g\nu g^{-1}=d(h\nu h^{-1})d^{-1}\in N_D.
\]

The middle conjugate lies in \(K^+\) by its normality in that source image. F.19's eight ambient normal generators therefore all have their conjugates in \(N_D\), proving

\[
\overline{\langle\!\langle K^+\rangle\!\rangle}_{D^+}=D^+.
\]

Passing to the abelianization proves that the actual image of \(K^+\) is the entire \(D^+_{\mathrm{ab}}\). The image is also full in every finite nilpotent quotient: a proper image would lie in a maximal subgroup, and the explicit upper-central-series argument proves that every such maximal subgroup is normal, contradicting normal generation. Compactness then gives the actual surjection onto the maximal pronilpotent quotient of \(D^+\).

1. EXACT CONFIGURATION SPACE AND TOPOLOGY

Fix a literal enumeration of labels by positive integers. A configuration
z=(z_i) is an infinite sequence of distinct complex numbers, with only
finitely many z_i in each compact planar set. Its counting measure is
mu_z=sum_i delta_(z_i). Write

 d_prod(z,w) = sum_(i>=1) 2^(-i) min(1, |z_i-w_i|).

For a countable compactly supported test family (phi_j) detecting vague
convergence, put

 d_V(mu,nu) = sum_(j>=1) 2^(-j)
              |integral phi_j d(mu-nu)| /
              (1+|integral phi_j d(mu-nu)|),
 d_Sigma(z,w) = d_prod(z,w)+d_V(mu_z,mu_w).

Thus the topology simultaneously requires coordinate convergence and
vague counting-measure convergence. These are the definitions at the
locators above. The point zero is allowed. The positive-integer sequence
(1,2,3,...) is a chosen base configuration for the fundamental groups,
not a restriction on every point of the configuration space. Neither
collar lemma requires that base configuration. The explicit collar
example below is even nonzero and has a fixed positive-integer tail.

2. COLLAR ASSERTIONS: COMPLETE DATA USED IN THE AUDIT

T25 Lemma 5.10:
R>0; epsilon>0; R/2+epsilon<R and 2R<3R-epsilon;
A={R<=|z|<=2R}, B={R/2<=|z|<=3R};
K compact metric; F:K->unordered configurations vague-continuous.
Its functions are

 u_in(x)=sup{|z|: z in F(x), R/2-epsilon<=|z|<R/2},
          with empty value R/2-epsilon;
 v_out(x)=inf{|z|: z in F(x), 3R<|z|<=3R+epsilon},
          with empty value 3R+epsilon.

The assertions are USC(u_in), LSC(v_out), and continuous separators
u_in<r_in<R/2 and 3R<r_out<v_out. The stated radial isotopy starts at
identity, fixes A and radii <=R/2-epsilon or >=3R+epsilon, is supported
in the two closed epsilon-collars, and sends radii r_in,r_out to R/2,3R
at time one, making the resulting configuration avoid boundary(B).

T26 Lemma 6.7:
K compact metric; F vague-continuous; R,epsilon>0;
u(x)=sup{|z|:z in F(x), R-epsilon<=|z|<R}, empty value R-epsilon.
It asserts USC(u). For closed L with F(L) avoiding the closed
epsilon-collar, it asserts continuous r with u<r<R on K\L and r=R
on L, and a radial isotopy supported in that collar, stationary on L,
starting at identity, whose time-one inverse takes radius R to r(x).

COUNTEREXAMPLE AND DIRECT SUPREMUM CALCULATION

Set K=[0,1/8] and

 F(t)={1-t} union {10,11,12,...}.

This is infinite, simple, locally finite, nonzero and labelled by
(1-t,10,11,...). Every compactly supported test function phi gives

 integral phi d(mu_(F(t))) = phi(1-t)+sum_(m>=10) phi(m),

where the displayed tail sum is fixed and finite. Hence F is
vague-continuous. Its only varying ordered coordinate is the first,
so it is also continuous in the exact ordered sum topology.

For T25 take R=2 and epsilon=1/4. The required inequalities are
1+1/4<2 and 4<6-1/4. The inner collar is [3/4,1) in radius. At t=0
it is empty; at every 0<t<=1/8 it contains exactly the point 1-t.
Consequently

 u_in(0)=3/4,
 u_in(t)=1-t  (0<t<=1/8),
 limsup_(t downarrow 0) u_in(t)=1>3/4.

For T26 take R=1, epsilon=1/4, and the allowed closed set L empty.
Its u is exactly the same function.

Moreover, any continuous r with u(t)<r(t)<1 would have r(0)>=1,
because the positive-t inequalities force liminf_(t downarrow 0)r(t)>=1.
This contradicts r(0)<1. Thus both semicontinuity and the required
continuous-separator assertion actually fail on these admissible data.

The printed proofs express {u<c} as a countably infinite intersection
of open compact-avoidance sets and then declare it open (T25 lines
1816-1828; T26 lines 2194-2206). Here c=7/8 gives
{t:u(t)<c}={0} on [0,1/8], which is not open. This computes the
specific failed openness step rather than merely questioning an
application of an insertion theorem.

3. TAIL-REPRESENTATIVE ASSERTION AND PAIR-WINDING COUNTEREXAMPLE

T26 Lemma 6.8 asserts:
for n>=1 and g in V_n=ker(p_n), a representative gamma exists with
gamma_k(t)=k for k<=n and gamma_m(t) outside K_(n-1) for m>n,
where K_r is the closed disk of radius r.

Use n=3. At the base configuration (1,2,3,4,5,...), fix all strands
except strand 4. For strand 4 use the following rational polygonal
lasso; pairs list (real part, imaginary part):

 tail:
 (4,0), (4,1), (5/4,1), (5/4,1/4);
 square:
 (5/4,1/4), (3/4,1/4), (3/4,-1/4), (5/4,-1/4), (5/4,1/4);
 reversed tail back to (4,0).

All intermediate points avoid the other positive integers. The square
is positively oriented and encloses 1 but not 2 or 3. The tail and
its reverse cancel in every winding calculation. Thus the continuous
ordered-pair maps

 (z_i)_i |-> z_4-z_1,       (z_i)_i |-> z_4-z_2

to C\{0} give windings 1 and 0. Only one coordinate moves in a fixed
compact set, so the lasso is continuous in d_Sigma. Its first three
coordinates are constant and its class g belongs to V_3.

Any representative demanded by Lemma 6.8 would have its first two
coordinates equal to 1,2 and its fourth coordinate z(t) outside
the closed radius-two disk. Then

 (s,t) |-> z(t)-(1+s),       0<=s,t<=1,

is a homotopy of loops in C\{0}, since |z(t)|>2 and 1+s lies in
[1,2]. The two windings would therefore be equal. They are invariant
under every based configuration homotopy through the two displayed
continuous maps, contradicting their values 1 and 0. This refutes
the actual representative assertion with its prescribed finite labels.

The rational polygon is independently checked in
code/teh_configuration_audit_certificate.py. No numerical winding or
floating-point approximation enters the proof.

4. AN INDEPENDENT INFINITE REALIZATION AND COMPLETENESS FAILURE

The target assertion is T26 Theorem 6.14:
g_(n+1) in g_n V_n for all n implies intersection_n(g_n V_n) nonempty.
Its displayed metric in Definition 6.17 records the largest matching
finite truncation by d(g,h)=2^(-(N(g,h)+1)) for distinct g,h;
Theorem 6.18 asserts completeness for that metric.

For every m>=3, let a_m be a based configuration loop moving only
strand m along the preceding type of lasso once around 1, zero
around 2, with all other positive-integer strands fixed. The
same tail construction with (m,0),(m,1) in place of (4,0),(4,1)
works. Set g_1=g_2=1 and g_n=a_3 a_4 ... a_n for n>=3.
Then g_(n+1)=g_n a_(n+1) and a_(n+1) lies in V_n. Every g_n is
an actual class represented by a finite concatenation of continuous
locally finite configuration loops.

We prove directly the needed restriction on any actual continuous
configuration loop z(t), 0<=t<=1:

 For each compact planar K, only finitely many labels meet K
 at any time of the loop.

Otherwise take labels m_i tending to infinity, parameters t_i
converging to t_*, and z_(m_i)(t_i) converging to a point p of K.
Local finiteness at t_* allows a nonnegative compactly supported
function equal to one near p whose support contains at most the
single limiting configuration point p. If p is absent at t_*,
its limiting integral is zero but the integrals along t_i are
at least one. If p is present with label j, coordinate continuity
and the extra labels m_i give integrals at least two while the
limiting integral is one. Each conclusion contradicts vague
continuity. This proves the restriction without importing T26.

Choose a closed disk containing both first-strand and second-strand
tracks of z, and enlarge it slightly. All sufficiently late
strands avoid this disk uniformly. For such an m, the formula

 (s,t) |-> z_m(t)-((1-s)z_1(t)+s z_2(t))

is nonzero throughout the square. It proves equality of the two
pair windings of strand m with strands 1 and 2.

A class in every g_n V_n would instead have winding 1 with strand 1
and winding 0 with strand 2 for every m>=3, by choosing n>=m.
This contradicts the restriction just proved. Thus the asserted
intersection is empty. In the displayed finite-truncation formula,
(g_n) is Cauchy because g_n^(-1)g_m lies in V_n for m>=n.
Convergence in that formula would force the impossible common
finite-truncation data. Consequently its claimed completeness fails.
This argument does not require injectivity of the map to the
finite-truncation inverse limit.

The same winding data also appear in T26 Construction 4.6 and
Proposition 4.9. The direct argument above establishes the conflict
without relying on either source proof. It does not assert that the
quotient topology on the topological fundamental group lacks some
other complete compatible metric.

5. FURTHER PROOF-CHECK BOUNDARY AND USABLE FINITE MAPS

then assumes S_k avoids the target disk for every L<k<n.
At n=n_start this already includes the intermediate earlier stages
L+1,...,n_start-1, whose avoidance has not been established by those
choices. This is an unproved induction input in the written argument,
not an explicit refutation of its injectivity conclusion. A single

have to be retained.

The finite-truncation local constructions in T26 Section 3 use
compactly supported finite-point ambient maps and give explicit

## Exact endpoint-path and frontier comparison

# Exact reductions after the fixed-frontier extension C63

C63 is complete and has passed root and independent C audits. This separate note records the remaining scope and an auxiliary fact relevant to the zero-dimensional local-centralizer case. It does not modify the registered C63 source or metadata.

## What the compact-family construction establishes at a nonfixed frontier

The global maps in C63's compact family are limits, in the actual global homeomorphism topology and all selected original source-cover topologies, of words in the original loop. They therefore preserve every original open orbit and fix every point fixed by the original generated group. Their projected point and inverse-point control is exact:

\[
K_{\rho,t}(x)\in\mathcal K\mathcal K^{-1}\mathcal K(x),\qquad
K_{\rho,t}^{-1}(x)\in\mathcal K^{-1}\mathcal K\mathcal K^{-1}(x).
\]

At a fixed frontier point, the compact evaluation set on the right is a singleton. At a nonfixed frontier point the proof supplies a compact evaluation set but does not identify it with one prescribed point. The construction also does not establish that arbitrary infinite-product limits preserve each individual nonopen original G-orbit. Consequently the same compactness argument does not, by itself, prove nonfixed-frontier continuity for the selected lift.

The continuous-selection proof was performed in the actual principal real line bundle. Its relative boundary conditions were the four homotopy-parameter faces, where the prescribed coefficients already belong to the original crossing intervals. A prescribed value on a physical nonfixed frontier has not been shown to satisfy an analogous lower-limit inclusion. No relative selection across that frontier is being asserted.

## Proved auxiliary fact: actual small paths move a point through an open neighborhood

This fact does not require a positive-dimensional local centralizer.

Take the countable collection of original open G-orbits. Retain their original universal covers and based lifted loop paths. As in C63, form the compatible product of the global plane homeomorphism group and the homeomorphism groups of those covers, with every map and inverse controlled on compact sets. Let L be the closure, in this exact product, of the subgroup generated by the labelled original loop. It is Polish. Its global values commute with the original operators, preserve every original open orbit, and fix the original G-fixed set. The covering and operator equations remain exact by closedness.

Let P(L) be the group of continuous paths σ:[0,1]→L with σ(0)=1, with pointwise multiplication and the compact-open path topology. It is Polish. A compatible complete metric on L gives completeness of the uniform path metric; uniform limits remain continuous and based. Separability follows by coding finite values from a countable dense subset and a uniform-continuity scale, selecting one actual path from every nonempty coded neighborhood. Pointwise multiplication and inversion are continuous on compact path-parameter sets.

Fix x in an original open orbit O. The action

\[
P(L)\times O\longrightarrow O,\qquad (\sigma,y)\longmapsto\sigma(1)y
\]

is continuous and transitive. Indeed, every original finite word carrying x to a prescribed point of O is the endpoint of an actual based word path: replace each original parameter t_j by s t_j and keep its inverse sign. This path lies in the labelled group L and retains all original source lifts.

The exact Polish orbit-open-map theorem already used in C30 therefore makes

\[
\operatorname{ev}_x:P(L)\longrightarrow O,\qquad
\sigma\longmapsto\sigma(1)x
\]

an open map. For every neighborhood U of the constant identity path in P(L), U·x is an open neighborhood of x in O. Thus every point of that neighborhood can be reached by some actual global operator-centralizing path satisfying all the controls defining U.

For example, U may require the global maps and inverses to move each point of one specified ambient compact set by less than ε at every time, and may simultaneously impose any finite collection of compact controls on the original source-cover maps and their inverses. All these are open conditions in the stated path topology. The resulting motions fix the original G-fixed set throughout and preserve every original open orbit.

This conclusion supplies existence of small actual paths for nearby endpoints. It does not supply a continuous choice of such paths as the endpoint varies, a local section of the evaluation map, or a lift of an arbitrary parameterized deformation. Those additional requirements have not been deduced from openness.

## Current remaining cases

The new fixed-frontier principal-fiber contraction leaves the prescribed-value problem at nonfixed frontier orbits. Open orbits whose full local centralizer is zero-dimensional also lack the principal one-dimensional fiber used by the selection argument. Their intrinsic contractions from C32 remain available, but a controlled global extension through all their frontiers has not been established. C12 remains open.


## Controlled fillings in the original planar domain

# Controlled filling inside the original planar domain

## Proved lemma

Let O be an open subset of the plane, D an open Euclidean disk, and U a connected component of O∩D. For every basepoint in U, the actual inclusion

\[
U\hookrightarrow O
\]

induces an injective homomorphism on fundamental groups. Consequently every loop in U which is null-homotopic in O has a based disk filling entirely inside U, and thus entirely inside the prescribed ambient disk D.

## Proof with the actual intermediate maps

Let γ be a based loop in U which is null-homotopic in O. Its compact image has an open neighborhood in U. A sufficiently fine polygonal approximation γ' and the straight homotopy on each small parameter interval remain in that neighborhood, fixing the basepoint. Choose the finitely many vertices generically if necessary, so that the polygonal image is a finite planar graph.

Take a sufficiently small compact connected planar regular neighborhood N of this graph inside U. It can be constructed as a finite union of small vertex disks and thin edge rectangles, followed by rounding corners. Its boundary consists of one outer Jordan curve and finitely many inner Jordan curves. Its bounded complementary components D_i are the open Jordan disks enclosed by the inner curves.

The closed outer Jordan disk containing N is contained in D. Indeed, the outer boundary is a compact subset of the convex disk D, and its entire bounded interior lies in the convex hull of that boundary: any point outside the convex hull is separated from it by a line and can be joined to infinity without meeting the boundary. The convex hull of a compact subset of the open Euclidean disk stays in that disk. In particular every inner disk D_i lies in D.

Fill into N precisely those D_i which are entirely contained in O, and call the resulting compact planar surface N'. Since each of their boundaries already belongs to N, this means adjoining the complete closed inner disk. Thus

\[
\gamma'\subset N\subset N'\subset O\cap D.
\]

The set N' is connected and meets U, so it is contained in the same component U. For every inner disk still unfilled, choose one point p_i∈D_i\O. These points are distinct and lie in the interiors of the remaining complementary disks.

The actual inclusion

\[
N'\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^2\setminus\{p_i\}
\]

is a homotopy equivalence, as can be seen by an explicit strong deformation retraction. For each remaining closed inner Jordan disk, choose a Schoenflies disk coordinate carrying p_i to the origin and its boundary to the unit circle. In the punctured disk use the radial homotopy

\[
(r,\theta)\longmapsto((1-t)r+t,\theta),\qquad 0<r\le1.
\]

For the exterior of the outer Jordan disk, use its Schoenflies exterior coordinate and the same formula for r≥1. All these homotopies fix their boundary circles pointwise. Together with the identity on N', they paste on the finite closed cover of the punctured plane to a strong deformation retraction onto N'. Every basepoint in N' remains fixed.

The null-homotopy of γ' in O is also a null-homotopy in the punctured plane, because every chosen p_i lies outside O. Applying the displayed deformation retraction gives a based disk filling of γ' in N'. Prepending the based polygonal approximation homotopy gives a filling of γ in U. This proves the asserted injectivity and the controlled filling statement.

## Exact scope for the frontier problem

The filled hull of a loop's image need not itself lie in O: a circle followed by its reverse in an annulus is already a null loop whose image surrounds an excluded point. The lemma above avoids that assertion. It produces a filling in the actual O and in any chosen open Euclidean disk containing the loop within one component of O∩D.

When original evaluation loops shrink uniformly to a fixed frontier point, choose disks with radii tending to zero that contain those loops. Their original ambient-null restrictions are null in O by C32, and each connected loop lies in one component of the intersection. The lemma therefore supplies disk fillings with the same vanishing ambient diameter. It does not provide a continuous selection of the fillings, a simultaneous configuration or edge isotopy, or an equivariant fragmentation of an arbitrary original loop.


## Exact principal-fiber extension of the interval argument

# Proved extension of C62 to the actual principal operator fibers

This note applies the already proved word triangle to another explicitly constructed foliation. It does not assert a lift of a moving base contraction or an ambient extension of the intrinsic C33 contraction.

Let O be an original open orbit of the loop-generated group G, and let C_O be the full local centralizer of G restricted to O with its actual compact-open topology. Suppose its dimension is one, and put A=C_O^0. C30 and C33 prove that C_O is a free proper Lie transformation group and construct a principal bundle

\[
\pi_0:O\longrightarrow B=O/A.
\]

Here A is the additive line or circle, B is a line or circle, and the pair of circles is excluded because O is noncompact. C33 supplies an actual section and the homeomorphism

\[
\Theta:A\times B\longrightarrow O,\qquad
\Theta(a,b)=a\,s(b),\qquad \pi_0\Theta(a,b)=b.
\]

## The original universal cover and its exact labels

Write η_A:R→A and η_B:R→B for the identity in a line factor and the specified quotient by Z in a circle factor. The displayed map

\[
p_*(u,v)=\Theta(\eta_A(u),\eta_B(v))
\]

is a covering from the simply connected plane, hence a universal covering. If p_O:X_O→O is the previously chosen universal covering, choose the point above Θ(0,0) in each cover. The unique based covering isomorphism χ:X_O→R² satisfies

\[
p_O=p_*\chi.
\]

It is a homeomorphism: the inverse is the unique based lift of p_* through p_O, and the two compositions are identity lifts with the same basepoint. Define the actual real quotient

\[
F=\operatorname{pr}_2\chi.
\]

Its connected proper fibers are horizontal lines in this explicit chart. The original deck labels are retained by

\[
\chi\delta\chi^{-1}(u,v)
 =(u+m_A(\delta),v+m_B(\delta)),
\]

where m_A or m_B is identically zero in each line factor, and the circle factor has its integer label determined by the original deck transformation. There is at most one circle factor. In particular

\[
F\delta=F+m_B(\delta).
\]

This is an equation for each original δ, not a replacement of its label by an unchosen covering generator.

## The original loop and all local operator components

Every f_t|O commutes with A. In the actual product chart its exact form is therefore

\[
(a,b)\longmapsto(a+\varphi_t(b),\psi_t(b)),
\]

as in C33.11. Its based source lift has the form

\[
\chi\widetilde f_t^O\chi^{-1}(u,v)
 =(u+\widetilde\varphi_t(v),\beta_t(v)),
\]

where β_t is the actual based real lift of ψ_t and is increasing. The fiber translation lift is fixed by the based source lift, including any nonzero integer accumulated in a circle fiber. No endpoint closure is needed for the C62 triangle argument. Every original deck map commutes with the source lift, by the same deck-valued commutator path used in C62.

Every q∈C_O normalizes its characteristic identity component A and hence preserves the A-orbit partition. Its induced map on B is the actual map of the quotient group C_O/A. C33 proves that this group acts freely and properly on B. A decreasing line or circle homeomorphism has a fixed point, so no decreasing element occurs in this induced group. Its source lifts consequently preserve F-fibers with increasing induced real base maps. The full affine fiber component equations in C33, including a negative conjugation coefficient on A, are retained; no such coefficient is discarded by the base orientation observation.

The original stabilizer H_O maps into C_O by restriction, with the precise kernel of C30.4. No identification of H_O with C_O is made. For an operator h transporting O to O', conjugation by h gives an actual topological group isomorphism C_O→C_O' and carries A-orbits to A'-orbits. Thus the principal partitions are transported along all original operator orbits. The projected global word comparison is automatically natural under h because h commutes with every f_t.

## Exact containment and uniform consequence

The source hypotheses used in the C62 proof are now all verified: the original cover, one actual product homeomorphism, a real quotient with connected proper fibers, the increasing induced base maps of the original lifted path, and the original deck equations. For any x∈O and two original prefix times whose values have exactly the same F-level, the compact interval I in that real fiber satisfies

\[
I\subset
\{\widetilde f_u^O(\widetilde f_v^O)^{-1}
  \widetilde f_a^O\widetilde x:0\le a\le v\le u\le1\}.
\]

Projection gives exactly

\[
p_O(I)\subset
\{f_u f_v^{-1}f_a(x):0\le a\le v\le u\le1\}.
\]

The inverse-path version is the projected word f_u^(-1)f_vf_a^(-1). For arbitrary varying dimension-one principal orbits with x_n→x, the one compact global word map gives the same uniform compact containment and same-G-orbit accumulation as C62, and complete shrinking when x is fixed by G.

This application does not require any actual global quotient to a nonopen orbit. In particular it applies when the full nonopen-target family is empty. ## Exact full-prefix fiber-hull selection obstruction

# The full prefix fiber hull need not admit a continuous base lift

This is a limitation of a particular lifting prescription. It supplies neither a failure of C12 nor a failure of lifting the base median itself. C62 remains applicable: the interval hulls considered here lie in the actual three-word images, which are a larger class of allowed values.

## The actual action and original quotient

For positive real λ and real c,d, let

\[
A_{\lambda,c,d}(x,y)=(\lambda x+c,e^d y).
\]

These maps form the closed plane group Aff⁺(R) × R. The coordinates of a homeomorphic limit are recovered by evaluating two points of the horizontal axis and two points of one vertical line; injectivity excludes a zero horizontal or vertical scale. Thus the group is closed with its stated Lie topology. It acts transitively on each open half-plane. Its only nonopen orbit is the horizontal axis B, on which its action is the affine line action.

Take the original operator group H to be the vertical scaling subgroup. Every displayed map commutes with H. On the upper half-plane O use the actual homeomorphism

\[
\chi:O\longrightarrow\mathbb R^2,\qquad
\chi(x,y)=(u,v)=(\log y,x).
\]

The action in this chart is exactly

\[
(u,v)\longmapsto(u+d,\lambda v+c).
\]

At the source point (x,y)=(0,1), the stabilizer consists of the maps with c=d=0. Its fixed set in the sole nonopen orbit B is {(0,0)}. Consequently the full family of actual nontrivial global quotients has exactly one member for that source label:

\[
\Phi(x,y)=(x,0),\qquad F(u,v)=v.
\]

No target or source period occurs.

## A based original loop

Interpolate each of λ,c,d linearly between these parameter values:

| Time | λ | c | d |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 1/6 | 5/4 | 1 | 2 |
| 1/3 | 3/4 | 1 | 3 |
| 1/2 | 3/2 | 1 | 2 |
| 2/3 | 3/2 | 1 | 3 |
| 5/6 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |

The positive values of λ make every interpolated map a homeomorphism. Write f_t for this based loop. It is already null-homotopic in the H-centralizer: replace its parameters by

\[
\lambda_r(t)=1-r+r\lambda(t),\qquad
c_r(t)=r c(t),\qquad d_r(t)=r d(t),
\quad 0\le r\le1.
\]

The subgroup generated by the loop is the whole displayed group. On the segment from 1/2 to 2/3, taking relative maps gives an interval of pure vertical translations in u; these generate the full vertical R. After cancelling this vertical factor, the first segment gives dilations about the line point -4. On the segment from 1/3 to 1/2, the base maps have the form v↦λv+1. Taking a relative map A_λ A_λ₀^(-1) gives v↦(λ/λ₀)v+1-λ/λ₀, which is a dilation about 1; its vertical factor is again cancelled by the already available vertical subgroup. An interval of positive dilation parameters generates every positive parameter, so both complete dilation groups are present. For equal parameters λ, the product of a dilation about p with the inverse dilation about q is the translation by (1-λ)(p-q). The two distinct centers therefore supply an interval of nonzero translations, hence every translation and the full affine group. The original open orbits and quotient just specified are thus exactly those of the loop-generated group.

## The median base and its full-prefix crossings

Fix the prefix length ρ=1/3 and the endpoint time T=5/6. For |v|<1/4 the running maximum of the real base path up to ρ is

\[
M(v)=1+v+\frac{|v|}{4}.
\]

Indeed the affine base coordinate is linear on every time segment, so its prefix maximum is the maximum at the vertices 0,1/6,1/3. The initial value v is below both other values near zero. The chosen endpoint is b_T(v)=v+3>M(v). C27's median base at these parameters is therefore exactly M(v).

For each source point (u,v), now allow **all** original times in the larger prefix [0,T], and take the hull in the real fiber F=M(v) of every crossing

\[
f_s(u,v),\qquad 0\le s\le T,\qquad b_s(v)=M(v).
\]

For 0<v<1/4, the crossing at time 1/6 has fiber shift 2. There is one further crossing on the segment from 1/3 to 1/2. Its fractional position on that segment is exactly

\[
\frac{(1+5v/4)-(1+3v/4)}{(1+3v/2)-(1+3v/4)}
=\frac23.
\]

The fiber shift there is 3+(2-3)(2/3)=7/3. Every other segment is strictly below or strictly above the level except for the already listed shared endpoints. Thus the full-prefix fiber hull has first-coordinate interval

\[
[u+2,u+7/3]\qquad(0<v<1/4).
\]

For -1/4<v<0, the prefix maximum is attained at time 1/3, with fiber shift 3. The segment from 2/3 to T later crosses the same level, but its fiber shift is identically 3. All remaining crossings are the same shared endpoint. Consequently the full-prefix fiber hull is the singleton

\[
\{u+3\}\qquad(-1/4<v<0).
\]

At v=0, all times from 1/6 through 2/3 lie at base level 1; their shifts fill [2,3]. The fiber hull at zero is [u+2,u+3].

## No continuous selection exists from these hulls

Any lift of the specified median base whose value at (u,v) is required to lie in this full-prefix fiber hull has fiber coordinate u+3 for every negative v close to zero, but has fiber coordinate at most u+7/3 for every positive v close to zero. Evaluating at the fixed source value u=0 proves that such a lift cannot be continuous at v=0. The larger hull at v=0 cannot change these incompatible one-sided limits.

This obstruction permits an arbitrary choice anywhere in the whole filled interval and allows the entire original prefix up to T, not just the shorter prefix that defines the running maximum. Thus pointwise interval filling alone does not supply a transverse continuous lifting rule. The explicit null-homotopy above shows exactly why this is a limitation of that rule rather than a failure of the underlying centralizer problem.

The affine equations, maximum comparisons, complete crossing list, and exact fiber shifts are checked symbolically in `code/prefix_fiber_hull_selection_certificate.py` and its adjacent JSON output. The continuity contradiction is the one-sided limit proof above.

Let `A = Homeo(X,S)` and let `u:Γ→A` be a strict action of an arbitrary discrete group. Put `H=u(Γ)`, `M=C_A(H)`, and base `M` at the identity. Let `N` be the weak automorphism groupoid of this action in the categorical group `Π₁A`, with its identity weak automorphism as base object. An automorphism of that base object is a loop class `z∈π₁(A,1)` satisfying the naturality equality

`u(γ) z u(γ)⁻¹ = z` for every `γ∈Γ`.

Consequently

`π₁N = π₁(A,1)^Γ`.

The comparison sends an actual centralizing loop to the same loop in `A`. Its exact map is

`ι_*: π₁(C_A(H),1) → π₁(A,1)^Γ`,

where `ι` is subgroup inclusion. The image lies in the displayed invariants because the representatives commute pointwise with every `u(γ)`. Finiteness of `Γ` is not used in this groupoid calculation. For a transporter based at any equivariant homeomorphism, translation by that homeomorphism identifies its based fundamental-group map with the corresponding automorphism-space map.

Every based loop in `C_A(H)` lies in `A⁰`, and every based homotopy does too. Thus its source is also `π₁(C_{A⁰}(H),1)`. ## 5. The compact-open topology and the universal-lift reduction

For this finite-type setup, restriction

`r: Homeo(X,S) → Homeo(X\\S)`

is a topological-group isomorphism for the compact-open topologies. Every homeomorphism of `U=X\\S` extends uniquely to the finite end compactification `X`, so `r` is an algebraic bijection. Restriction is continuous. For completeness, continuity of its inverse can be checked directly. Choose disjoint connected target end neighborhoods `W_j` of diameter below a prescribed uniform tolerance in `X`, and let the complementary target core `C` be compact in `U`. Choose a compact source core `K` large enough that `f₀⁻¹(C)` lies in its interior, and connected source tails `V_i` outside `K` with `f₀(V_i)⊂W_{σ(i)}`. The compact-open condition `f⁻¹(C)⊂int K` is open because inversion is continuous in the homeomorphism group of the locally compact, locally connected surface `U`. Choose one point `z_i` in each `V_i` and impose the open conditions `f(z_i)∈W_{σ(i)}`. Connectedness now gives `f(V_i)⊂W_{σ(i)}`: the image avoids `C` and contains that prescribed point. This controls the extensions at all ends uniformly. Ordinary compact-open control on the complementary compact core controls the rest of `X`. Translating this neighborhood argument from `f₀` to any homeomorphism proves continuity of `r⁻¹`.

The canonical-lift map in the paragraph after C.12 is consequently a continuous injective homomorphism for the same topology and same ambient group used throughout Part C:

`j:A⁰→Homeo(Ũ)`, `p j(f)=f p`, `j(f)δ=δj(f)` for every deck transformation `δ∈π₁U`.

Centre-freeness gives uniqueness of the commuting lift, and proves the exact equality

`j(C_{A⁰}(H)) = j(A⁰) ∩ C_{Homeo(Ũ)}(H̃)`,

where `H̃` is the group of all lifts of elements of `H`. In particular, based centralizer loops lift to closed loops. This equality provides no null-homotopy in that intersection. For arbitrary `H`, metric geodesic interpolation need not commute with `H̃` and need not consist of homeomorphisms. Those are separate required properties, and neither has been established by the lift comparison.
